title: Stay in the tray on Wayland when the window closes
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Fixes #4

## What was wrong

On Wayland, closing the window with "Keep running in the tray" on did nothing. The launcher cancelled the close and asked winit to hide the window, which winit 0.30 can't do on Wayland (`set_visible` is empty there).

## What changed

On Wayland, where the window can't hide, closing to the tray now closes the window and keeps the process and the tray icon. A tray click, "Show ArtCraft Launcher" or a second launch opens a new window onto the same state. Windows, macOS and X11 keep hiding the one window, as before. XWayland counts as X11, since the check reads the display handle winit opened.

How:

- The UI state, its backend and the tray icon now live in `main` (`Launcher`), outside any window. `Shell` is one window onto it.
- `main` loops over `eframe::run_native`. eframe keeps the winit event loop and reuses it, so a window can open again after one has closed.
- With no window, a loop in `main` keeps calling `LauncherUi::logic`, so update checks, notifications and the tray tooltip carry on. It sleeps until something wakes it or until the time `logic` itself asks for with `request_repaint_after`.
- Each window gets its own egui context, and `LauncherUi::attach` moves the UI to it (fonts, image loaders, theme). One shared context does not work: a new window's renderer never receives the textures the context already handed out ("Missing texture: Managed(0)", blank window).
- A tray click with the window open closes it to the tray on Wayland. "Show" with the window already open asks the desktop for attention, since winit can't focus or unminimize a Wayland window.
- A `--hidden` start at login goes to the tray on Wayland too. The window is mapped for a moment first (50 to 100 ms here), because the saved settings and the tray icon come with the first window.

The packaging text ("lives in the system tray") stays true. No new dependency. The branch includes `main` at e8c4b3d (merge commit).

title: Keep the verified download when the install step fails
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
When the install step failed after a download had finished and passed its checksum, the launcher deleted the file, so the next Install downloaded 100 MB or more again. The usual cause is dismissing the password prompt. Fixes #5.

The file is now kept when the install step fails. The next Install checks it against the published SHA-256 again and goes straight to installing when it matches; a file that no longer matches is downloaded again. While a file is waiting, the main button reads "Retry install" (or "Retry update to <version>") and the "…" menu has "Download again", which throws the file away first.

![The CADCraft card with "Retry install" as its main button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/craft-launcher/9d2e4885792f86eb04a8f59950325a7771b5f34a/retry-install.png)

![The card's menu with "Download again"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/craft-launcher/9d2e4885792f86eb04a8f59950325a7771b5f34a/download-again.png)

Both are test snapshots (`ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_SNAPSHOTS`), not a running launcher.

**Notes**

- A download that could only be checked by size (a release with no checksum) is still deleted after a failed install, because there would be nothing to check it against later.
- On `main` the cleanup deletes any finished file older than a minute each time it runs (startup, every five minutes, and when the window regains focus), including while the installer is running. Finished files now age out after 30 days, the same as paused downloads, and reusing a kept file marks it as just used so the cleanup cannot remove it during the install.
- The backend reports the kept file with a new `Event::ReadyToInstall`, sent from the same place as `Event::Paused`, and again after a check for updates and after a settings change, since both can change which file would be installed. `start_job` and `run_as_root` are untouched.

title: Queue system installs so several apps can install at once
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Installing several apps at once on Linux no longer fails with "error 100", and "Update all" usually asks for the password once or twice, down from once per app. It does not reach the single prompt that #6 lists as expected: the first download to finish starts a call by itself, and the rest usually share the next one (a download that finishes later still goes into a further call). Fixes #6

The cause: each install started its own `pkexec apt-get` (or dnf, zypper, rpm), so they fought over the package manager's lock and each asked for the password.

What changed:

- Installs and removals wait their turn for the system's installer. A waiting app shows "Waiting for another app…" with a Cancel button; once its call has started it can no longer be cancelled.
- On Linux, the waiting apps go into one privileged call (`apt-get install a.deb b.deb`), so one password covers them. Dismissing that prompt cancels all of them. If the call fails, an app found installed at the new version afterwards reports success; the others report the error and say to try them one at a time. The launcher does not retry by itself, because that would ask for the password once per app.
- `apt-get` gets `-o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60`, so for up to 60 seconds it waits for another package tool to release the dpkg lock. This needs apt 1.9.11 or newer and covers only the dpkg and frontend locks. The card shows "Installing…" during that wait, with no separate message.
- The launcher's own update waits for other installs to end before it replaces itself and restarts, and no new install starts once it has begun.
- On Windows, `msiexec` runs one at a time, so a second install waits and no longer stops with error 1618. This part has never been run.

```
...
test queue::tests::jobs_that_wait_together_share_one_call_per_command ... ok
test queue::tests::installers_never_run_at_the_same_time ... ok
test queue::tests::a_job_arriving_mid_install_waits_then_runs ... ok

title: Centre the app name and tagline on the icon in the grid and the table
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Fixes #7

## What was wrong

The app name and tagline sat off-centre beside the app icon: 12 pt too high in the table, 10 pt too low in the grid.

Both used `ui.vertical` next to the icon. A row in egui only centres a widget whose height it knows when the widget is allocated, but `ui.vertical` is given the whole remaining space and fills it from the top. In the card, the name line was also as tall as a button (`interact_size.y`, 30 pt), so the three lines were taller than the 54 pt icon.

## What changed

- `centered_lines` in `crates/ui-egui/src/views.rs` allocates the text block at the height of its lines, so the row centres it like any other widget. The table and the card both use it.
- In the card, the name line is now as tall as its text. The three lines come to within half a pixel of the icon's height, and the name and tagline sit 4.5 pt closer together.
- The space under the card's icon row goes from 10 to 22 pt. This is a deliberate choice: the text used to overhang the icon by 12 pt, and the larger gap keeps the status pill and version line where they are. With the 10 pt gap they would move up 12 pt.
- The table's name label is explicitly single-line, like the tagline. Its column already truncated it, so nothing changes on screen.

Card height, row height, the NEW badge and the Website/GitHub links are unchanged.

Known follow-up, not in this PR: `title()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs` has the same pattern, a 40 pt icon beside a `ui.vertical`.

From the UI test snapshots at 2x. The lines mark the top and bottom of the icon.

title: UI tests: stop the intermittent segfault in parallel runs
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
Fixes #12

The UI tests no longer create a GPU device unless they are asked for screenshots, so a normal `cargo test` or `cargo xtask ci` never enters the Vulkan loader, where the crash was.

## Cause

It is a bug in the Vulkan loader, not in this repository, wgpu or the GPU driver: [KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Loader#1863](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Loader/issues/1863). The loader walks its global list of devices under one mutex while `vkCreateDevice` and `vkDestroyDevice` change that list under another. It was fixed by [Vulkan-Loader#1866](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Loader/pull/1866), which is in Vulkan SDK 1.4.350 but not in 1.4.341, the version Ubuntu 26.04 ships.

The tests set it off because `harness()` called `.wgpu()`, which builds a wgpu device for every test straight away. Nine tests then create, use and destroy a device at the same time on separate threads. In a debug build wgpu names each Vulkan object it creates, and that naming call is the one that walks the list.

<details>
<summary>Backtrace (gdb, loader 1.4.341.0, two crashes at the same address)</summary>

```

title: Default wgpu to Direct3D 12 on Windows to fix startup crash on hybrid AMD laptops
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Summary

On Windows the launcher now asks wgpu for Direct3D 12 with GL as the fallback, instead of wgpu's default list, which starts with Vulkan. `WGPU_BACKEND` still overrides the choice, and other platforms keep wgpu's defaults.

Without this, `artcraft-launcher.exe` dies on startup with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xC0000005) on an ASUS ROG Strix G513QY (Ryzen 9 5900HX with integrated Radeon graphics + Radeon RX 6800M). The exe is a GUI-subsystem binary, so nothing is printed and `cargo run` only reports the exit code.

## Root cause

The crash is inside AMD's Vulkan driver, not in our code:

- The Windows Application event log puts every crash in `amdvlk64.dll` from the RX 6800M driver package, at the same fault offset each time.
- The laptop runs two AMD driver packages at once: the integrated Radeon is on the OEM driver (30.0.13002.13003, Dec 2021) and the RX 6800M on Adrenalin (32.0.21045.5002, Aug 2026). AMD's installer does not touch the OEM iGPU driver, so this state is permanent and common on OEM hybrid laptops.
- Both packages register a Vulkan ICD, and the 2021 one also claims the RX 6800M, so the Vulkan loader reports the 6800M twice. wgpu picks the first discrete adapter, which is the 6800M through the 2021 user-mode driver on top of the 2026 kernel driver, and the process dies right after the surface is configured, before the first frame.
- Pointing `VK_DRIVER_FILES` at only the 2026 ICD makes Vulkan work, so the mix of the two drivers is the trigger. Disabling every Vulkan layer (Steam, OBS, Epic overlays) changes nothing.
- `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` and `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` both run fine on the same machine.

Direct3D 12 is Windows' native API and sidesteps third-party Vulkan ICDs and overlay layers entirely, which makes it the safer default for a launcher that must never crash.

## Changes

- `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs`: new `wgpu_options()` that sets `Backends::from_env().unwrap_or(DX12 | GL)` on Windows and returns wgpu's defaults elsewhere.
-…

title: Windows installer: choose the install folder, optional desktop shortcut; 0.1.2
author: bflatastic
body:
## What

- **Choose the install folder.** The Windows setup wizard gains a folder page between Welcome and Ready, with the stock path checks and the Change… browser. The default is still `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft Launcher`. The install stays per-user (no UAC prompt), so the page notes to pick a folder you can write to.
- **Optional desktop shortcut.** A "Create a desktop shortcut" box sits on the same page. It's a normal MSI component, so uninstall removes it. It goes before Install rather than on the Finish page so Windows Installer tracks the shortcut.
- **Updates keep both choices.** The folder and the shortcut choice are recorded under `HKCU\Software\Learning Machines LLC\ArtCraft Launcher`. The next version reads them, so a self-update (`/passive`) lands in the same folder and keeps the choice.
  - The box starts ticked on a first install.
  - Updating from 0.1.0 or 0.1.1, which never asked, adds no desktop icon.
  - `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT=0/1` on the command line wins.
- **Self-update finds non-default installs.** `self_update.rs` now recognises an MSI install by the folder the MSI records (`InstallDir`), not only the default one.
- **Version 0.1.2.**

## Checks

- `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, clippy, tests, wasm.
- Built the x64 MSI locally. `wix msi validate` (all ICEs) reports no errors; the warnings are the expected same-version upgrade, shortcut-to-exe component and per-user ones.
- Opened the wizard: Welcome → folder page (folder, Change…, note, desktop box) → Ready, then cancelled.
- The Windows ARM64 workflow now installs twice on real Windows: with the defaults (default folder, Start Menu and desktop shortcuts, choice recorded) and into a chosen folder with `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT=0` (no desktop shortcut). It checks each uninstall removes everything.

title: Add UI localisation (i18n) with a Russian catalog
author: MaksPV
body:
Every user-visible string in the interface is now looked up from a per-language catalog at render time instead of being compiled in as English. English stays the source of truth and the lookup keys, so a missing row falls back to English rather than failing.

**i18n module** (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/`) — `t`, `tr`, `tr_ctx` (one English word needing different translations), `tr_id` (command-id keyed menu items with English fallback), `trn` (plurals), `fmt` (`{name}` placeholders filled after the lookup), `message`/`msg` (status and error text), and the `tl!` macro for literals at call sites.

**Russian catalog** (`ru.tsv`) — covers the whole interface in clean-room, international Russian, with East Slavic plural forms (one/few/many), month abbreviations and a day-month-year date template. Product and app names (ArtCraft Launcher, the Craft App Suite, PhotoCraft…SoundCraft) stay in English, as do GitHub, Discord and the URL labels.

**System language detection** — the UI follows the system locale by default: `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_LOCALE`/`LANG`/`LC_ALL` and friends on Unix, `defaults read -g AppleLocale` on macOS, the registry UI language on Windows, and `?lang=` then `navigator.languages` on the web. Settings › Language overrides it (auto / English / Русский); the choice applies on the next frame and persists.

**Dates and relative times** — `core` stays pure and wasm-safe: `time::ago_kind` classifies a timestamp without words, `month_short_en` provides the month source key and `civil_from_unix` the calendar parts, so `Oct 8, 2026` renders as `8 окт. 2026` and `4 min ago` as `4 минуты назад` without core depending on the UI crate.

**Deliberately untranslated** — the trademark notice stays in English, as legal text.

**Tests** — catalog tests cover parsing, placeholder symmetry, plural-form counts per language and duplicate keys; the UI integration tests force English so they don't depend on the machine's locale.

title: Use the ArtCraft API's release feed, with GitHub as the fallback, and rate-limit it
author: echelon
body:
## What

The launcher now gets every app's latest release from one request to ArtCraft's API (`GET https://api.storyteller.ai/v1/craft_apps/release_info`, served by storyteller-web). It asks GitHub only for apps the feed can't vouch for.

- **Release feed (`crates/core/src/feed.rs`).** Parsing is lenient: missing or malformed fields never fail the whole feed. Entries older than 24 h fall back to GitHub. Repo renames are followed. Download URLs must point at the app's own GitHub releases.
- **Fallback policy.**
  - On the very first poll, the launcher tries the API once, then asks GitHub so the window fills.
  - Until every app has loaded once, GitHub is asked fairly eagerly (every 5 minutes per app).
  - After that, GitHub is asked only when the API has seriously failed (3 checks in a row and an hour without an answer), and then at most hourly per app.
- **Footer.** It says where the answers came from: "Checked just now · using ArtCraft API", "using GitHub" or "using ArtCraft API and GitHub".
- **Notices.** Announcements show as dismissible banners and alerts as a popup. Both are restyled for the new theme.
- **Rate limits on the API (`crates/native/src/feed_throttle.rs`):**
  - At most **1 request a minute** once the first load is over.
  - **Up to 10 a minute during the first load**, front-loaded. The gaps double after each failure (2 s, 4 s, 8 s, …), so a struggling server sees clients ease off fast. The first load ends at the first answer or after 10 requests.
  - **Failures back off** 2, 4, 8 … minutes, up to an hour, with jitter. A 5xx `Retry-After` is honoured.
  - **HTTP 429 throttles hard.** The launcher waits at least 15 minutes, doubling with each 429 in a row up to 6 hours. It never retries sooner than `Retry-After`, and adds up to 50% jitter so a thundering herd doesn't come back in step.
  - The backoff is saved to `cache/feed-throttle.json`, so relaunching doesn't skip it.

title: Verify HTTPS certificates with the OS instead of a copy of its root store
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #42

On some Windows PCs every release check fails with `invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer`, so every app shows "Not available here". We load the Windows root store once with rustls-native-certs, but Windows only adds many roots when it's asked to verify a chain, so the root GitHub needs can be missing.

This switches ureq to its `platform-verifier` feature (rustls-platform-verifier). Windows and macOS now check each chain themselves and fetch missing roots. Linux still reads the system store. No bundled root list gets pulled in (checked `cargo tree` for Windows, macOS and Linux targets), so the CDLA concern in the Cargo.toml comment still holds.

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` passes, and so does the ignored live test that downloads a real release asset. I ran both on Linux only and haven't built on Windows or tried it on an affected PC.

title: macOS: install only apps signed by the Craft team, at the release's v…
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
Closes #50.

On macOS, a Craft App (or the launcher's own update) now replaces the installed copy only if:

- **it's signed by the Craft team** (`DJ6XS33FX8`, Learning Machines LLC): `codesign --verify --deep` with a requirement that pins the Developer ID team. An unsigned or ad-hoc-signed bundle, or one from another developer, is refused. It works offline.
- **it's the release's version**: the bundle's version must match the release. A bundle that reports only `CFBundleShortVersionString` matches a pre-release with the same numbers.

Both run on the staged copy after `ditto`, before `swap_into_place`. On failure the staged copy is removed and the installed app is left as it was.

**Changes**
- `install.rs`: `macos::TEAM_ID`, `macos::Expect` (team + version; `Expect::release(&release)` in production), and a `check()` step in `copy_app`. `install_dmg` takes the `Expect`.
- `self_update.rs`: passes `Expect::release(release)`. Its existing test builds an unsigned bundle, so it passes `Expect { team: None, version: None }`.
- New messages follow the existing style: "the app isn't signed by its developer, so it wasn't installed" and "the app inside isn't version X, so it wasn't installed".

**Tests** (macOS only)
- `only_the_teams_signature_passes`: unsigned and ad-hoc-signed bundles fail, and a crafted team id can't widen the requirement.
- `the_bundle_must_be_the_releases_version`: matching, newer, older and pre-release cases, each leaving the installed copy as expected.
- `an_unsigned_update_leaves_the_installed_copy_alone`
- `a_real_craft_app_carries_the_teams_signature` (`#[ignore]`, run with `CRAFT_APP=…`). Passes on PhotoCraft 0.6.0, LightCraft 0.5.0, VectorCraft 0.8.0 and ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.3. I also checked each one's signature after the `ditto --noextattr` copy.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Show GitHub's limit notice only while it actually holds details back
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #44

The footer warning came straight from the last time GitHub's API said no, and two things kept it up when it shouldn't be.

A 403 or 429 was treated as "hourly limit reached" until `x-ratelimit-reset`. GitHub sends that header on every answer, so a secondary limit (quota left, "retry in 60 s") turned into up to an hour of warning. Now the reset time only counts when `x-ratelimit-remaining` is 0. Otherwise we wait for `Retry-After`, or a minute on a bare 429, as GitHub's docs say.

The notice also stayed up for the rest of that hour after the ArtCraft feed had answered every app, when nothing was missing. Now a check only reports the limit if some app had to come from the release pages or the saved cache.

I couldn't reproduce the reporter's exact setup and didn't run it on macOS. New unit tests cover how a refusal is read (a local server sends a 403 with quota left, `Retry-After: 60` and a reset 50 min out; it failed before at 3000 s and passes now) and when the footer notice is shown. `cargo xtask ci` passes on Linux. The web build reads GitHub's 403s the same way it did before and isn't touched here.

title: Fix "Show in Explorer" opening Documents instead of the app's folder
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #39

The Craft apps' MSIs install to C:\Program Files\<App>, so the path we pass to Explorer has a space in it. We built the argument as one `/select,<path>` string and gave it to `Command::arg`, which wraps any argument with a space in quotes. Explorer got `"/select,C:\Program Files\PhotoCraft\photocraft.exe"`, didn't recognise the switch, and opened its default folder, which is Documents. Paths without a space (and the macOS and Linux code paths) were fine, which is why this only showed up on Windows.

Now the argument is built as `/select,"<path>"`, with only the path quoted and forward slashes turned into backslashes, and passed with `raw_arg` so Rust doesn't quote it again.

The argument building is a plain function with unit tests (path with spaces, without spaces, with forward slashes), and `cargo xtask ci` passes on Linux. I haven't run it on Windows: the `raw_arg` call is Windows-only code that I couldn't compile or try here, so it would be good if someone clicked "Show in Explorer" on an installed app before merging.

title: Pick the Linux package format from os-release, not from tools on PATH
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #21

The launcher decided which system package it could install by looking for programs on PATH. If apt-get and dpkg were there it offered .deb, and it only offered .rpm when dpkg was missing. Fedora can have apt and dpkg installed (mmdebstrap, debootstrap and similar tools pull them in), and on such a system the launcher downloaded the .deb and ran apt-get on it, with .rpm ruled out completely.

Now the format comes from /etc/os-release. If ID or ID_LIKE says debian or ubuntu, the launcher uses .deb. If it says fedora, rhel, centos, suse or opensuse, it uses .rpm. Either one also needs pkexec and the matching tools. Arch and unknown distros get no system package, so they get the AppImage. After the system package, AppImage now comes before Flatpak, because a Flatpak bundle needs a Flathub runtime and an AppImage doesn't. You can still pick Flatpak in Settings. Installing a .deb now fails with a clear message when there's no apt-get, and removing one falls back to dpkg -r.

The parsing and the choice are pure functions in core/src/distro.rs, with unit tests for Fedora (with and without apt installed), Rocky, openSUSE Tumbleweed, Ubuntu, Mint, Arch and an unknown distro. cargo xtask ci passes. I haven't run it on a real Fedora machine.

title: Find AppImages outside ~/Applications and add a menu entry when installing one
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #14
Fixes #37

#14 has no details, so I went by the code. AppImages the launcher installed itself are found fine, both from its record and by scanning ~/Applications. What it missed were AppImages put anywhere else, or renamed. Detection only looked in ~/Applications and only matched the exact release file name. So a copy in Gear Lever's ~/AppImages, one in ~/.local/bin, or one named photocraft.appimage (Gear Lever renames them like that) showed as not installed.

Detection now also looks in ~/AppImages and ~/.local/bin, ignores the case of the extension, and still only matches the release name (photocraft-0.6.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage) or the bare app name. A copy the user keeps somewhere else is never deleted.

For #37, installing an AppImage now writes ai.storyteller.<app>.desktop into $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications. The app's icon from assets/app-icons is copied to icons/hicolor/128x128/apps. Exec is quoted per the Desktop Entry spec, and Categories and StartupWMClass come from each app's own .desktop file. title: Use the system proxy for GitHub and downloads
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #30

The launcher now picks a proxy once at startup and uses it for every request. The proxy environment variables (HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY) still win, as before. Without them it reads the OS setting:

- Windows: the manual proxy under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings, either a single `host:port` or the per-protocol `http=...;https=...` form (the https entry is preferred), plus the ProxyOverride bypass list.
- macOS: the HTTPS proxy from `scutil --proxy`, falling back to the HTTP one, plus the exceptions list.
- Linux and FreeBSD: environment variables only, which is how most desktops pass the proxy on. GNOME/KDE settings aren't read.

Loopback always goes direct. The log says which proxy is used (host and port, no credentials).

Not supported: automatic configuration (PAC scripts and WPAD), SOCKS-only Windows settings, and `<local>` in the Windows bypass list. If you use a PAC file, set HTTPS_PROXY instead.

ureq has a `win-system-proxy` feature, but it treats the whole ProxyServer value as one address, so the per-protocol form breaks it. That's why the parsing is done here.

Testing: unit tests for the Windows ProxyServer and ProxyOverride formats, the scutil output and the bypass list; `cargo xtask ci` passes on Linux. I haven't compiled or run the Windows and macOS code paths, and haven't tried it behind a real proxy.

title: Let a newer launcher take over from an older one that's already running
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #29

The window in the screenshot isn't 0.1.2. It has the "Open Source Tools for Creatives, Makers, and Builders" tagline and the old header buttons, which only 0.1.0 had, and it offers "Download" where a portable 0.1.2 (portable.txt next to the exe) would offer "Update and restart". So a 0.1.0 launcher was still running in the tray. Starting the 0.1.2 exe hit the single-instance port, told the running copy to show its window and exited. That old window still had the update it found earlier in the day, when 0.1.1 was the latest. The version check itself is fine: is_newer(0.1.1, 0.1.2) is false, and the 0.1.2 binary reports 0.1.2.

The fix makes the single-instance handoff check versions. A second start now sends its version, and the running launcher replies with its own. If the new start is newer, the running launcher quits and the new one takes the port, waiting up to 10 seconds for it. If the old launcher is busy downloading or installing, it shows its window and doesn't quit. A start that's the same version or older shows the running window like before. Launchers from before this change (0.1.3 and older) hang up without replying and can't be asked to quit, so the new start runs anyway. Old launchers still send a plain "show", and that still works.

Testing: unit tests in single_instance.rs run the handshake over loopback. They cover a newer start replacing an older running launcher (the #29 case), same or older starts showing the window, a pre-handshake "show", a pre-handshake running launcher that hangs up, and garbage input. cargo xtask ci passes. The old code had no version handshake, so the new tests don't compile against it. They don't fail at an assertion. I haven't tried it in the real app on Windows, macOS or Linux, so the quit-and-take-over step (window close, process exit, port freed) and the case with a 0.1.3 launcher in the tray are untested.

title: Add an option to install Craft apps from local repos instead of GitHub
author: khutchings
body:
## Summary

Adds an option to point ArtCraft Launcher at Craft apps built from locally stored repos instead of GitHub. With it, a developer can install and update the whole suite from their own checkouts, for example to try unreleased changes or to work without GitHub.

It's opt-in and changes nothing by default: unless `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE` is set, the launcher behaves exactly as before.

```sh
cargo xtask local serve --sync-every 1h        # pull, build and serve the local apps
ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787/ cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher
```

## Launcher

- **`ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE`** points the launcher at a local mirror. While it's set, each check reads the mirror's `release_info.json` (the same shape as ArtCraft's feed). Downloads under the mirror are accepted, entries never count as stale, and GitHub and ArtCraft's API are never asked.
- **Loopback only:** `http://127.0.0.1:`, `localhost:` or `[::1]:`. Any other value is ignored with a warning, and links containing `..` are dropped.
- **Checksums still apply:** every download is still checked against its SHA-256 before it's installed.
- **Mirror down:** if the mirror isn't running, each app reports "the local mirror didn't answer" rather than falling back to GitHub.

## `cargo xtask local` (std-only, like the rest of xtask)

- **`sync`** runs `git pull --ff-only --recurse-submodules` in each sibling app checkout (`../photocraft`, `../wordcraft`, …). It then packages each app whose version isn't mirrored yet with that app's own `packaging/<os>/package.sh`, and files the result under `<mirror>/<app>/<version>/` with `SHA256SUMS.txt` and notes from `git log`.
  - Builds happen in a scratch folder and are moved into place only when complete.
  - A failed pull or build is reported per app, and the other apps carry on.
  - Options: `--only`, `--no-pull`, `--rebuild`, `--arch`, `--keep`, and `-- <package.sh args>`.
- **`--every-commit`** builds every new commit…

title: Windows: one permission prompt for Update all, then silent installs
author: KattKnight
body:
Closes #67.

## What this does

On Windows, **Update all** now asks for permission once, then installs every app in the background. Before, each app got its own UAC prompt and its own Windows Installer window, one after another.

- **One prompt per batch.** MSI jobs join a batch (`msi_batch.rs`) before their downloads start. Once no MSI is still downloading, everything ready goes to one call, so Update all becomes one batch however long each download takes. A job that fails, pauses or is cancelled while it downloads leaves the batch. A job waiting for the others shows *Waiting for another app…* and can still be cancelled.
- **The call is the launcher, started elevated** (`elevated.rs`): `artcraft-launcher.exe --install-msis <results> (<msi> <sha256>)…`, through `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, the same way `self_update.rs` already starts `msiexec`, so no `unsafe` code is needed. The UAC prompt names ArtCraft Launcher. The program and its arguments go to PowerShell through the environment, so nothing needs PowerShell quoting.
- **Silent installs.** The helper runs `msiexec /i <msi> /qn /norestart` for each file in turn and writes each result to a results file as it goes. The launcher reads that file to move the cards from *Waiting for permission…* (new `JobPhase::Permission`) to *Installing…* and to each app's own result. One failed app doesn't fail the others, and declining the prompt cancels the batch as a dismissed prompt does today.
- **A running app is checked for again** after its download and before the batch, so `/qn` never leaves files waiting for a reboot.

Uninstalls, macOS and Linux are unchanged. Batches and uninstalls still take turns through `INSTALLER`.

### The golden rule

*Never run an installer with elevated rights silently; tell the user what is about to happen.* The user still starts every install or update, and still answers the UAC prompt, while the cards say *Waiting for permission…*. "Silent" only means no Windows Installer windows.

title: Quit from the tray even when the window is minimized and gets no frames (#31)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #31.

**Cause.** The tray's Quit goes through the window: the tray handler queues `TrayAction::Quit` and requests a repaint, `Launcher::tick` (run from `eframe::App::logic`) picks it up, and `Shell::quit` sends `ViewportCommand::Close`. A minimized window gets no frames on KDE/Wayland, so none of that runs until the window is restored. That matches the report: Quit does nothing, and the launcher closes as soon as the window comes back.

**Fix.**
- Picking Quit in the tray now sets a `quit_pending` flag on the `Waker` before the action is queued, then wakes the UI as before.
- When `Launcher::tick` takes up the tray Quit, it clears the flag, and the usual quit runs: `Shell::quit` with a window, `TrayStep::Quit` in the windowless tray loop.
- A short watchdog thread checks the flag after `QUIT_GRACE` (2 s). If no tick has taken the quit up by then (the minimized window got no frame), the launcher logs a warning and exits.
- Nothing changes when the window is visible, hidden, or closed to the tray: a tick takes the quit up straight away, and the watchdog does nothing.

The flag is set before the action reaches the channel, so a tick that runs in between can't clear it early and leave a stale flag for the watchdog.

**Trade-off.** The fallback exit happens only when the window can't run a frame. That path skips eframe's final save on close, so a setting changed after eframe's last autosave (every 30 s) and before minimizing may be lost. The normal quit path is unchanged.

**Tests.** `a_tray_quit_nobody_took_up_ends_the_launcher` checks the flag logic: a pending quit that nobody took up is reported once, and one that a tick took up is not reported.

title: Enhance flatpak support with sandbox installing as fallback
author: donotfx
body:
Inside the launcher's own Flatpak, nothing could be installed: apt, pkexec and the flatpak tool are all outside the sandbox, and an AppImage cannot mount there, so the only format on offer could not run there either. The launcher now detects a sandbox (`FLATPAK_ID`) and offers the release tarball first: the app is unpacked into the launcher's own folder and run from there with `HOME` pointed at a `home/` folder beside it, so every Craft App's settings, projects and caches stay in the sandbox instead of the host's home folder. An update swaps only `bin/` and `share/`, and removing an app keeps its settings, the way a package manager keeps a removed app's data. Outside a sandbox nothing changes.

Both Flatpak manifests also gain `--socket=pulseaudio`, for SoundCraft's audio. `cargo xtask ci` passes, including four new tests, and the bundle was built with SoundCraft 0.4.0 installed from its tarball inside the sandbox: checksum verified, no missing shared libraries, and its config landed under `apps/soundcraft/home/.config`.

title: linux: prefer Flatpak if available and support host execution from Flatpak sandbox
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary

1. **Match default package format to launcher format**:
   - Running from the **Flatpak launcher** (`process::in_sandbox()`) defaults to **Flatpak** packages first (clean per-user install, sandbox isolation, full desktop menu integration).
   - Running from the **AppImage launcher** (`$APPIMAGE`) defaults to **AppImage**.
   - Running the **base Linux launcher** (native distro install or direct binary) defaults to native system packages (`.deb` / `.rpm` via polkit) if available, then Flatpak, then AppImage.
   - Users can still customize their preferred package format in the launcher Settings.

2. **Support Flatpak sandbox execution via `flatpak-spawn --host`**:
   - The launcher's Flatpak manifest already requests `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak` and `--filesystem=home` specifically to manage and run host software.
   - When running inside a Flatpak container (`FLATPAK_ID` / `/.flatpak-info`), `flatpak` commands (`install`, `uninstall`, `list`, `info`, `run`) are delegated to `flatpak-spawn --host flatpak`.
   - Host binary execution (`launch_binary`), file opening (`open`), and process check (`is_running`) similarly delegate to the host via `flatpak-spawn --host` when sandboxed, allowing host applications to run with host FUSE and desktop integration instead of failing silently inside the container mount namespace.
   - `detect.rs` now properly detects installed Flatpak apps when the launcher itself is sandboxed.

Fixes #75, Fixes #24.

title: Automatically download and install updates when available
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary

Adds an opt-in setting under **Settings > Updates** to automatically download and install updates for installed apps and the launcher as soon as they are detected.

- **Settings Toggle**: Added `Automatically download and install updates` checkbox (`Settings::auto_update`, defaulting to `false`).
- **Auto-Installation**: When enabled, any installed app with `AppStatus::UpdateAvailable` automatically queues `Command::Install`.

title: linux: fix detection of system package installs
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves #97.

### Summary
When installing an application via system package (`.deb`, `.rpm`, etc.), the launcher sometimes still showed "INSTALL" instead of "OPEN" even though the package installed successfully and its desktop entry was created.

### Changes
1. **RPM filtering in `ours`**: Added `InstallSource::Rpm` to the candidate filter in `linux::packages()`, which was previously omitted.
2. **Bundle ID candidate names**: Added `app.bundle_id()` (`ai.storyteller.<app>`) to `candidate_names()` for `Deb` and `Rpm` packages alongside short stems.
3. **Multiarch qualifiers**: Stripped architecture qualifiers (such as `:amd64`) in `parse_dpkg()`.
4. **AppImage environment pollution**: Sanitized `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and other AppImage runtime environment variables in `process::command()` so system package manager query tools (`rpm`, `dpkg-query`, `pacman`) run cleanly against host system libraries.
5. **Desktop entry & binary fallback**: If package manager query tools fail, time out, or run in a constrained environment, `linux::detect()` now falls back to inspecting the installed desktop entry and system binary, extracting the version via `--version`.

title: fix(wgpu): prefer D3D12 (incl. WARP) over GL on Windows
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes storytold/artcraft#2087 - Launcher crashes immediately on startup on legacy GPU hardware (Intel HD 4000 + AMD Radeon HD 7600M) with wgpu error "Failed to wait for GPU to come idle before reconfiguring the Surface".

## Problem

On Windows machines with legacy GPUs that have no hardware Direct3D 12 support (Intel HD 4000, AMD Radeon TeraScale), the launcher crashes before the window appears. wgpu's default adapter selection ranks WARP (Microsoft's software renderer) last, so it picks the OpenGL adapter. The old GL driver fails `Surface::configure`, and wgpu panics before any app code can handle it.

## Solution

Custom adapter selector that ranks **any D3D12 adapter (including WARP CPU renderer) above OpenGL** on Windows when `WGPU_BACKEND` is unset.

- Machines with hardware D3D12 GPUs: unchanged behavior (still pick hardware)
- Legacy GPUs without D3D12: now use WARP instead of crashing
- `WGPU_BACKEND` env var still overrides for manual control

## Implementation

**Changed:** `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` (+51/-3)
- Added `native_adapter_selector` hook in `wgpu_options()`
- New `adapter_rank()` function: D3D12 adapters rank before GL, preserving wgpu's device type order otherwise
- Graceful error if no adapter can draw to the window (no unwrap/panic)

**Test:** `warp_beats_a_gl_gpu_but_not_a_d3d12_gpu` verifies ranking logic

## Quality Gates

✓ `cargo fmt`  
✓ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`  
✓ `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher` (21 passed)

## Trade-offs

**Accepted:** Old GPUs with *working* GL drivers will also get WARP (CPU-based rendering). The reporter confirmed WARP is usable for the launcher UI, and this population (pre-2013 GPUs) is small and has equally old/fragile GL drivers.

**Alternative considered but not implemented:** Vendoring egui-wgpu to catch the error and retry (~160 lines, ongoing maintenance burden on every egui upgrade). Not justified for this edge case.

## Verification

Reporter confirme…

title: fix(wgpu): prefer OpenGL on Intel integrated GPUs where D3D12 fails
author: mahmagha
body:
## Summary

Fixes #111 - Launcher crashes on startup on machines with Intel HD/UHD Graphics 500/600 series (Intel Core 6th?10th Gen) with wgpu validation error `Shader translation error: The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057)`.

## Problem

PR #105 introduced `adapter_rank()` on Windows to prioritize any Direct3D 12 adapter (including WARP) ahead of OpenGL to fix pre-D3D12 legacy GPUs (like Intel HD 4000).

However, on Intel Gen 9/9.5 integrated graphics (e.g. Intel UHD Graphics 620, HD Graphics 530/630):
- A hardware Direct3D 12 adapter is present, so `adapter_rank()` selects `Backend::Dx12`.
- When creating `egui_pipeline` under D3D12, shader translation under wgpu's default FXC compiler fails with:
  `Shader translation error for stage ShaderStages(VERTEX | FRAGMENT): The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057)`
  causing an unhandled panic on startup.
- Meanwhile, their OpenGL driver is fully featured OpenGL 4.6 and runs the launcher smoothly with full hardware acceleration (`WGPU_BACKEND=gl` works).

## Solution

Refined `adapter_rank()` on Windows:
1. When an Intel integrated GPU has a Direct3D 12 driver on the system (`has_intel_d3d12`), rank its **OpenGL** adapter ahead of D3D12 and WARP so it uses full hardware acceleration and avoids the D3D12 shader translation error.
2. Pre-D3D12 legacy GPUs without a hardware D3D12 driver (like Intel HD 4000) continue to rank **WARP** above broken legacy OpenGL, preserving PR #105's fix.
3. Hardware D3D12 discrete GPUs (NVIDIA/AMD) remain the top preference.

## Tests
- Updated `warp_beats_a_gl_gpu_but_not_a_d3d12_gpu` to verify WARP still beats legacy GL on pre-D3D12 GPUs.
- Added `intel_gl_beats_intel_d3d12_and_warp_when_d3d12_driver_exists` to verify Intel GL ranks ahead of Intel D3D12 and WARP when hardware D3D12 exists.

title: macOS: set the notification bundle id so no 'Where is use_default?' picker appears (#95)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #95.

**Cause.** On macOS, notify-rust 4.18.2 sends notifications through mac-notification-sys 0.6.15. If the application was never set, the first `show()` calls `ensure_application_set()`. That function runs the AppleScript `get id of application "use_default"`, and macOS replies with the "Where is use_default?" app picker. The launcher never called `notify_rust::set_application`, so this lookup ran on every first notification. The reporter saw it mostly with the window closed to the menu bar, where background update checks send the notifications.

**Fix (macOS only).** `DesktopHost::notify` now calls `claim_notification_identity()` before it shows a notification. That function calls `notify_rust::set_application(APP_ID)` (`ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`, the same id used for the window, settings and Windows notifications) exactly once and keeps the result in a `OnceLock`.
- The library accepts only one `set_application` call, and every later call returns "already set". Keeping the first result means repeated notifications don't hit that error.
- If setting the id fails (for example, a dev build that LaunchServices doesn't know), the failure is logged once. The `use_default` lookup is still skipped, because the library treats even a failed call as "application set". The notification then falls back to the library's default sender instead of showing the picker.
- Windows and Linux/BSD are unchanged.

**Test.** `notification_identity_is_claimed_once` (macOS only) checks that a second call returns the same result as the first. Without the memo, the second call returns the library's `AlreadySet` error. The test does not require `Ok`, because setting the id fails on machines where the launcher app is not installed. CI has no macOS job, so this test runs only on a Mac.

title: Linux: restore menu entries for legacy AppImage installs

body:

Refs #48.

title: Linux: re-add a missing menu entry for recorded AppImages on rescan
author: Qreepex
body:
## Problem
Reported in #118: installing WordCraft (0.5.0) — and on the affected system equally PhotoCraft (0.7.0) — as an AppImage via the launcher wrote **no** `.desktop` file or icon, and `installed.json` recorded `"files": []`. For other AppImage installs this works, so `integrate_into()`'s best-effort writes can fail silently (they only `log::warn!`, and the launcher AppImage has no visible log). The app then never appears in the desktop's menu, and nothing ever retries the integration.

## Fix
Two parts:

1. **Self-healing rescan** (`backend.rs`): after detecting installed apps, a launcher rescan now checks each app whose record is a launcher-installed AppImage with empty `files` (the exact witness of "integration never wrote anything"). If the AppImage still exists but no menu entry does, it runs `integrate_into()` again and persists the written files back into the manifest. Entries written by the app itself are respected (only a *missing* entry is added).

2. **Comment + helpers** (`install.rs`): the desktop-entry half of `integrate_into()` is split into `menu_entry()` so the rescan path and `integrate_into()` share one implementation; `menu_entry_exists()` checks whether an entry is there. A comment documents that an icon failure must not stop a later update from writing the entry.

## Testing
- `cargo check` / `cargo clippy` / `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native` passes (98 passed).
- Verified the scenario locally on the affected CachyOS machine: with a record containing `files: []` and no `.desktop`, launching a patched binary adds the missing entry and updates `installed.json` with the written files.

Fixes #118

title: macOS: keep the bundle's icon in the Dock while the launcher runs
author: valenfys
body:
Fixes #32.

**Cause.** eframe sets the app icon at runtime. On macOS it calls `setApplicationIconImage` with whatever `ViewportBuilder::with_icon` was given, which here is the 256 px PNG, or egui's own logo when no icon is given. That replaces the bundle's `.icns` in the Dock with a raw bitmap and skips macOS's icon treatment. This is why the icon looks right in Finder and in the Dock before launch, then changes once the app is running.

**Fix.** On macOS, pass `egui::IconData::default()`. eframe treats the empty icon as "don't set one", so the bundle's `.icns` stays. Windows and Linux still get the PNG.

**Trade-off.** An unbundled `cargo run` on macOS now shows the generic program icon in the Dock. Packaged builds show the real one.

**Testing.** `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher` passes. Built and packaged with `packaging/macos/package.sh --arch aarch64` (ad-hoc signed) and launched it on Apple Silicon: the Dock icon stays the bundle's `.icns` while the app runs, matching Finder and the Dock before launch.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across Craft Launcher to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for Craft Launcher.

title: Detect PdfCraft installs made by its PrintCraft-named MSI
author: matttitmarsh
body:
**Problem.** On Windows, a PdfCraft install made by its early MSI, which shipped as PrintCraft up to 0.2.1, shows as not installed: the launcher offers Install instead of Update, shows no installed version, and can't uninstall it.

**Cause.** Windows detection accepts an uninstall entry only when its DisplayName equals the app's current name ([`detect.rs:153`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/c5b073f5f7f6076ba8ac688d7965c1b098ece432/crates/native/src/detect.rs#L153)), and looks for the exe only as `pdfcraft.exe`, in `App Paths`, the install folder and `Program Files\PdfCraft` ([`detect.rs:173-191`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/c5b073f5f7f6076ba8ac688d7965c1b098ece432/crates/native/src/detect.rs#L173-L191)). `uninstall_msi` uses the same lookup ([`install.rs:1028`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/c5b073f5f7f6076ba8ac688d7965c1b098ece432/crates/native/src/install.rs#L1028)). The PrintCraft MSI registers DisplayName `PrintCraft`, installs `printcraft.exe` into `Program Files\PrintCraft` and registers `App Paths\printcraft.exe`: see `printcraft.wxs` at storytold/pdfcraft v0.1.0 and v0.2.1. `pdfcraft.wxs` at v0.4.0 switches to PdfCraft with the same UpgradeCode. The catalog already knew the old asset stem (`former_ids`, [`catalog.rs:49`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/c5b073f5f7f6076ba8ac688d7965c1b098ece432/crates/core/src/catalog.rs#L49)), but Windows detection didn't use it.

**Fix.** `CraftApp` gains `former_names` (PdfCraft: `PrintCraft`) and `names()`, alongside `former_ids`/`stems()`. Entry matching accepts any of the app's names, still exactly and still only from Learning Machines LLC. The exe is looked up under every stem in `App Paths` and under every name in Program Files, current first. A first commit moves the two decisions out of the `#[cfg(windows)]` registry code into pure functions with no behaviour change, so they're tested on every platform.

title: macOS: open disk images reliably, and say why when they won't open; 0.2.1
author: bflatastic
body:
﻿## What

Installing or updating an app on macOS could fail with nothing more than **"couldn't open the disk image"**. That's the error users are reporting.

- **A new mount folder for every install.** Before, every install of an app mounted its image at the same `mount-<app>` folder in the cache. An attach that was interrupted or timed out could still be holding that folder, so later installs failed.
- **No duplicate checksum pass.** The attach uses `-noverify`: the download's SHA-256 is already checked against the release, and on a large image hdiutil's own pass could run past the time limit. The limit is also raised to 5 minutes.
- **The real reason in the message.** When an image still won't open, or the app won't copy, the error now quotes the tool, e.g. "couldn't open the disk image: Resource temporarily unavailable", so reports can be diagnosed.
- **Full tool paths.** `hdiutil`, `ditto` and `codesign` are run as `/usr/bin/…`, because a launcher started from Finder or at login gets a minimal `PATH`.

This builds on the one-at-a-time attach with retries already on main (8d76d19). The launcher's own macOS self-update installs through the same code, so it gets all of this too.

`process::run` is a sibling of `capture` that returns the helper's error message, and `capture` is now built on it. It has tests on Windows and Linux.

## Checks

- `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, clippy, tests, wasm.
- New `process::run` tests cover a helper's own error, a silent failure and a success.
- The macOS-only code isn't built by PR CI (no macOS runners on PRs). The next release build compiles it and packages, signs and verifies the macOS app before anything is published.

title: Windows: an option to use portable apps instead of the MSI
author: voodoo66
body:
Settings > Installing on Windows > "Use portable apps instead of the installer" downloads each app's portable zip, checks it against its SHA-256 like any download, and unpacks it into apps\<app> beside the launcher's exe (C:\craft-launcher\apps\photocraft). An Architecture menu picks the build: this PC's own by default (native first, then emulated), or exactly the one chosen, from the architectures this PC can run.

While the option is on, the launcher handles portable copies only: Windows Installer installs aren't detected or updated, and don't block a portable install. Off, nothing changes. Toggling it detects again (a toggle during a running detection pass is no longer lost).

- The installed version comes from artcraft-launcher-install.json, which the launcher writes into the app's folder (version, tag, architecture, zip). Without it the copy still shows, with an unknown version.
- An update unpacks beside the old copy and swaps the folders, then moves across whatever the old copy had that the new zip doesn't ship (settings or data kept beside the exe). A failed swap puts the old copy back; leftovers of an interrupted update are kept, never deleted.
- Uninstalling deletes the whole apps\<app> folder, only that folder, and the dialog warns that anything the app saved in it goes too.
- Unpacking (new dependency: zip 9, Deflate only, pure Rust) refuses entries outside the folder and links, and caps the zip at 50,000 files and 8 GiB unpacked, counting the bytes that actually come out.

New strings are translated in every complete catalog; the README's install table has a row for portable apps.

Fixes #136

On Linux the tray showed a number like "619651" instead of the app name.

The cause is in tray-icon 0.25.1. `TrayIconBuilder::new()` sets the id to `TrayIconId::new_unique()`, which is `format!("{}-{}", std::process::id(), COUNTER.next())` (src/tray_icon_id.rs), so for us it's "<pid>-1". We never called `with_title`, so the title stayed empty. The ksni backend (src/platform_impl/ksni/mod.rs) passes both straight to the StatusNotifierItem: `Tray::id()` returns that id, and `title()` and the tooltip title return the empty string. When a tray host gets no Title it falls back to the Id, so you see "61965-1" (or "619651" once the dash is dropped). That also explains why the number changes on every launch.

The fix gives the icon a fixed id, "artcraft-launcher", and the title "ArtCraft Launcher" on Linux and the BSDs. ksni builds the D-Bus name from the pid and its own counter, not from our id (ksni 0.3.6 src/service.rs), so a fixed id can't clash. Windows and macOS keep tray-icon's defaults. On macOS the title would be drawn as text next to the menu bar icon, and Windows doesn't support titles.

Testing: a unit test checks that the builder's id is "artcraft-launcher" on Linux/BSD and is still tray-icon's pid-based default on Windows/macOS. It failed before the fix (`left: "546358-1"`). fmt, clippy -D warnings and the workspace tests pass on Linux.

Not verified: I didn't run it on a real Linux desktop (KDE or GNOME with the AppIndicator extension), so I haven't seen the tray show the name. One small side effect: with no updates pending, the KDE tooltip may now say "ArtCraft Launcher" twice, as title and description.

title: linux: fix Flatpak bundle updates, serialize installs, filter detection by arch, and add status logging
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
1. **Flatpak bundle updates failed with 'already installed'** (Fixes #151):
When updating an already-installed app (or the launcher itself) using Flatpak bundles, `flatpak install --user -y --noninteractive --bundle <file>` fails because Flatpak requires `--reinstall` to install a bundle over an existing installation.
Passing `--reinstall` allows Flatpak to install the bundle over the existing installation cleanly when updating, while still performing a normal install if the app is not yet installed.

2. **Clean error reporting instead of hardcoded Flathub message** (Fixes #152):
Switched `PackageKind::Flatpak` from `.status()` to `.output()`. If Flatpak installation fails, the launcher now reports the actual error message returned by Flatpak rather than unconditionally displaying `Flatpak couldn't install the bundle (it needs the Flathub remote for its runtime)`.

3. **Serialize Flatpak bundle installations** (Fixes #153):
Flatpak installations now run through the installer queue (`root.queue.alone`) rather than running concurrently across background threads. This prevents lock contention on the OSTree repo and socket/DNS failures when multiple apps are updated simultaneously.

4. **Filter Flatpak detection by host architecture** (Fixes #154):
Passed `--arch=<host_arch>` to `flatpak list` and `flatpak info` in detection. Previously, if any foreign-architecture builds were installed on the host, `flatpak list` would list them and the first match could be picked regardless of architecture, causing the launcher to detect an outdated foreign build and stay in an update loop.

5. **Strict architecture asset selection across all package formats**:
Confirmed and added unit tests in `artcraft-launcher-core` verifying that release asset selection strictly matches the host platform architecture across all package formats (AppImage, deb, rpm, Flatpak, and tar.gz) and never allows foreign architecture builds or unintended fallbacks.

title: fix(windows): use FXC shader compiler to avoid stray dxcompiler.dll
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes storytold/artcraft#2103 - Launcher fails to start on some Windows systems with error "DXIL.dll not found".

## Root Cause

wgpu 30's default shader compiler setting (`Dx12Compiler::Auto`) searches for `dxcompiler.dll` on the system DLL search path. If it finds an **old or incomplete copy** (e.g., from an SDK or another app) that's missing its matching `dxil.dll`, every shader compilation fails and the launcher never opens a window.

The workaround (copying both DLLs to the launcher directory) worked because the exe's directory is searched first, overriding the broken system copy.

## Solution

Force wgpu to use **FXC** (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`), Windows' built-in shader compiler, instead of searching for `dxcompiler.dll`.

**One-line change:**
```rust
setup.instance_descriptor.backend_options.dx12.shader_compiler = Dx12Compiler::Fxc.with_env();
```

- FXC ships with Windows - no DLL dependency issues
- Most users already run this path successfully (when no `dxcompiler.dll` is found)
- `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` env var still allows override

## Why Not Bundle the DLLs?

- Would add ~25 MB to installer and portable zip
- Complex licensing (LLVM + Microsoft redistributable)
- Needs changes to WiX, CI, ARM64 build, attribution
- FXC solves the problem without the overhead

## Testing

Cannot build for Windows on macOS. Needs Windows CI to verify:
- Should compile without warnings
- Should start successfully on systems with broken `dxcompiler.dll` on PATH
- `RUST_LOG=debug` should log "Using FXC for shader compilation"

## Trade-offs

**Risk:** PR #112 reports FXC failures on some Intel 6th–10th gen integrated graphics. However:
- Those machines already use FXC today (no `dxcompiler.dll` found)
- This change only affects users who currently have a working DXC setup

## Implementation

**Changed:** `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` (+7/-1)

✓ `rustfmt --check` passes on changed file  
⚠️ Cannot run clippy for Windows target on macOS (needs MSVC headers)

title: Linux: draw on the desktop's GPU, not always the discrete one
author: abszar
body:
Refs #69

## Problem

egui asks wgpu for the **high-performance** adapter. On a hybrid laptop in PRIME **on-demand** mode (the Ubuntu default with the NVIDIA driver), the display server runs on the integrated GPU, but the launcher renders on the discrete one. Every frame is then copied between the GPUs (PRIME), and while the window is resized it ends up showing stale or garbled frames and can stop drawing until it is resized again. That is the "ghost frames" / freeze in #69.

## Change

On Linux and the BSDs, `wgpu_options()` now sets `PowerPreference::None` unless `WGPU_POWER_PREF` is set. With no preference, wgpu keeps the adapters in the order Vulkan lists them and takes the first compatible one. Mesa's device-select layer (`VK_LAYER_MESA_device_select`, shipped with `mesa-vulkan-drivers`) lists the display server's GPU first, or the one `DRI_PRIME` picks. So the launcher draws on whichever GPU drives the screens, with no cross-GPU copy:

| PRIME mode (`prime-select`) | Adapters as wgpu lists them | Before (HighPerformance) | After (None) |
|---|---|---|---|
| on-demand: X on Intel | Intel, NVIDIA, llvmpipe, GL Intel | NVIDIA (cross-GPU copy) | **Intel** |
| nvidia: X on NVIDIA | NVIDIA, Intel, llvmpipe, GL NVIDIA | NVIDIA | **NVIDIA** |

`WGPU_POWER_PREF=high|low|none` still overrides the default, and `WGPU_BACKEND` still works as before. Windows and macOS keep their current behaviour.

## Testing

Machine: XMG FOCUS E23 (Clevo NP5xSNx), i9-13900HX, RTX 4060 Laptop (driver 580.178.04-open) + Intel RPL-S (Mesa 25.2.8), Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46 on X11, 4K monitor on HDMI (wired to NVIDIA) + 1440p laptop panel.

- Reproduced on `main` (0.2.1) in on-demand mode with scripted resize bursts (`wmctrl`, 150 resizes, 20 ms apart), comparing the title bar with a screenshot taken before the burst:
  - NVIDIA (current default): window stale or garbled after the burst in 2 of 12 runs.
  - Intel (`WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`): 0 of 10 runs.
  - GL on Intel (`WGPU_BACKEND=gl`): 0 of 3 …

title: Linux X11: give the window a background, so resizing leaves no trails
author: abszar
body:
Refs #69. Companion to #164; the two PRs are independent of each other.

## Problem

winit creates its X11 windows without a background (no `CWBackPixel`, so the background is `None`). When the window grows, the area it gains keeps whatever was in that memory (earlier frames, other windows' pixels) until the app presents its next frame. While an edge is being dragged, that shows up as trails behind the edge (the screenshot in #69). winit 0.30 has no option to set an X11 window background.

## Change

- New `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/x11_background.rs` (Linux and the BSDs only). It opens a separate pure-Rust `x11rb` connection, looks up the window's visual, and sets the window's `background_pixel` to the launcher's background colour (`Tokens::bg`). The X server then fills newly exposed areas with that colour, which reads as the window's empty page.
- `Shell` keeps the X11 window id (from `cc.window_handle()`, Xlib or Xcb only) and applies the colour once when the window opens, then again whenever the light/dark appearance changes.
- Wayland windows are left alone: the compositor waits for the app's next buffer anyway. A failure only logs at debug level; the worst case is the current behaviour.
- `x11rb = "0.13"` is added as a Linux/BSD dependency. It's already in `Cargo.lock` through winit, and it needs no `unsafe` here (`unsafe_code = "forbid"` still holds).
- Pixels are computed from the visual's channel masks: 24-bit TrueColor, 16-bit 565, and 32-bit ARGB (where alpha is set to opaque).

## Testing

- New unit tests: `only_x11_windows_get_an_x11_background` and three `x11_background::tests` for the pixel encoding (24, 16 and 32 bit).
- Rebased on `main` at 0f295d4 (2026-10-14): `cargo xtask ci` passes fmt and clippy, `cargo xtask wasm` passes, and `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher` passes (42 tests).

title: Windows: compile DX12 shaders with FXC
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Windows the launcher exited before its window appeared with "Parent device is lost". wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` it finds on the DLL search path. The launcher ships none, and without a matching `dxil.dll` DXC warns that the DXIL is unsigned. wgpu treats that warning as a compile error, its indirect-validation pipeline fails and the device is lost. `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` worked because GL never touches DXC.

The fix: `wgpu_options` now sets the DX12 compiler to FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) through a small `pin_dx12_compiler` helper. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still overrides it for troubleshooting. It applies whether or not `WGPU_BACKEND` is set. Same approach as storytold/gridcraft#382, storytold/cadcraft#613 and storytold/lightcraft#484.

I left GL in the Windows default (`DX12 | GL`), unlike storytold/soundcraft#34. Here GL is a deliberate fallback (bee2ffc, #105): the adapter selector ranks every D3D12 adapter, WARP included, ahead of GL, and only takes GL when no D3D12 adapter can present to the window. Dropping it would leave those machines with no adapter at all. The AMD `atio6axx.dll` crash in GL instance creation hasn't been reported against the launcher. If it is, that's a separate change.

Tested with a unit test (`dx12_shaders_compile_with_fxc_unless_asked`) that starts from `Auto` and checks the helper leaves FXC, and that an explicit `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` choice is kept. It failed before the change and passes now. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

Not verified: I built on Linux only, where `wgpu_options` for Windows (`#[cfg(windows)]`) isn't compiled (no Windows target installed here), so Windows CI is what checks the call site. Nobody ran it on a Windows machine.

Fixes #126

title: linux: only run pacman when the pacman database exists, so an unrelated pacman on PATH is not launched (#158)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #158.

On Linux, every detection pass ran `pacman -Q` without checking that this system uses pacman. On Debian-family systems with the Pac-Man game installed, `pacman` on `PATH` is `/usr/games/pacman`, so the launcher kept opening the game.

Now `linux::packages()` runs `pacman -Q` only when pacman's local database, `/var/lib/pacman/local`, exists. Every pacman install has this directory, and other distros do not. If it is missing, pacman is never run, so neither the game nor a missing binary gets launched.

Of the two options in the issue, I picked this check. `/etc/os-release` would miss Arch derivatives that don't list `arch` in `ID_LIKE`. Running `pacman --version` first would still start the unrelated program. Detection for dpkg, rpm and Flatpak works as before. The only other `pacman` call is `pacman -R` for uninstalling, and that only runs for apps that detection already found through pacman. This change is Linux-only. FreeBSD detection never calls pacman.

Test: `pacman_is_only_queried_where_its_database_exists` checks the new `pacman_db_present` helper against a temporary directory, both before and after the `local` directory is created.

title: Fix system theme matching on Linux Wayland
author: vbasky
body:
On Linux Wayland, choosing Match System leaves the launcher dark even when the desktop appearance portal reports light. Read the portal color scheme in a background worker, subscribe to changes, and supply it to eframe raw input so egui follows the desktop. Explicit Light and Dark preferences retain precedence; missing or unsupported portal preferences preserve the native fallback.

The worker uses bounded method calls and retries portal failures without blocking the UI. Both ReadOne and legacy Read responses are supported.

Validation:
- cargo xtask ci (formatting, workspace Clippy, workspace tests, WebAssembly checks)
- Regression tests for light/dark transitions, explicit preferences, unknown values and legacy variant wrapping
- cargo test -p artcraft-launcher running_desktop_portal_reaches_egui -- --ignored against a live light-mode desktop portal
- cargo build --release -p artcraft-launcher; installed locally and verified portal detection reports Light

title: linux: support self-update and restart for Flatpak launcher
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary

When ArtCraft Launcher is running inside a Flatpak container, self-update was previously unavailable because `detect()` returned `None` for sandboxed environments. As a result, the launcher displayed a "Download" button (which downloaded an AppImage to the user's host downloads folder) rather than "Update and restart", and automatic updates did not trigger for the launcher itself (see #182).

1. **Flatpak installation detection**:
   - Added `Install::Flatpak` to `Install` enum in `self_update.rs`.
   - In `detect()`, if running inside a sandbox and `process::is_flatpak_available()` (via `flatpak-spawn --host`), detect as `Install::Flatpak`.
2. **Bundle update**:
   - Downloads the platform `.flatpak` bundle release asset.
   - Reinstalls the bundle with `flatpak install --user -y --noninteractive --reinstall --bundle <bundle>` through the host portal via `flatpak-spawn --host`.
3. **Relaunch after exit**:
   - Spawns a detached host helper via `flatpak-spawn --host` that identifies the container's host PID / instance ID.
   - The host helper monitors the PID until the existing launcher process exits, then executes `flatpak run ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`.
4. **Download fallback**:
   - Updated `launcher_download` in `backend.rs` and `views.rs` to prefer `.flatpak` bundles when running inside a Flatpak container.
5. **Tests**:
   - Added test coverage in `self_update.rs` for Flatpak asset picking and metadata/PID parsing.
   - All tests, clippy, fmt, and wasm checks pass (`cargo xtask ci`).

title: Fix doubled 'installed' on PdfCraft and SoundCraft cards

title: Accessibility/UI: follow the OS's animation setting
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

With Windows' "Animation effects" switched off, the launcher still glided each notch of the mouse wheel over several frames, faded its dropdowns in (the Sort dropdown, for one) and animated a card on hover. egui does the first two by default, and nothing in the launcher asked the OS.

## What changes

The shell now says what the OS wants (`Host::reduce_motion`), and the UI asks it about once a second while it draws, so toggling the setting takes effect without a restart.

With fewer animations asked for:

- **The mouse wheel scrolls at once.** egui 0.36 has no switch for its wheel smoothing, but it applies a trackpad's small steps as they come. Each wheel event is rewritten as a run of such steps in the shell's `raw_input_hook`.
- **Dropdowns, tooltips and dialogs appear without a fade**, and scrolling to a place jumps there (`style.animation_time`, `style.scroll_animation`).
- **A hovered card shows at once**: the rule along its top and the icon's rise no longer take 0.3 s.

Progress bars and spinners keep moving, since they show that work is going on. With animations on, nothing changes.

## Where the setting comes from

| Platform | Source |
|---|---|
| Windows | `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION`, read as bit 33 of `UserPreferencesMask` in the registry (`SystemParametersInfoW` needs `unsafe`) |
| macOS | `NSWorkspace`'s `accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion` |
| Linux / BSD | The XDG settings portal over D-Bus: its `reduced-motion`, GNOME's `enable-animations`, KDE's `AnimationDurationFactor`. Followed on a thread, so the UI never waits for D-Bus |
| Web | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

Animations stay on wherever the setting can't be read, which is today's behaviour.

## Testing

**Automated**

- `cargo xtask ci` passed on the first commit (fmt, clippy, tests, wasm), as did CI's `--locked` clippy steps. The second commit only adds tests; fmt, `--locked` clippy and the UI crate's tests were rerun for it.

title: Dialogs: keep the uninstall prompt at its own size, not the last dialog's
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #88: the uninstall prompt opened stretched almost to the edges of the window, with its two buttons floating in the middle, and stayed that way. Still reproducible on 0.3.2 after opening Settings (or an app's release notes) and then choosing Uninstall… from an app's … menu.

## Cause

Every dialog was shown through one `egui::Modal` with the same id, `"dialog"`. egui lays an area out in the size it had the frame before (`Area::content_ui` uses the remembered `state.rect()` as the max rect), so after Settings had been open the prompt's first frame got Settings' height. The prompt's button row was `ui.with_layout(Layout::right_to_left(Align::Center), …)` placed straight in the column; a horizontal layout with vertical centring fills the whole height available and the placer records that whole frame as used, so the content claimed all of the leftover height, the area remembered that size, and it never shrank back.

## Change

- Each dialog gets its own area id (`Dialog::key()`), and each feed alert too, so a small prompt starts from its own size rather than the last dialog's.
- The uninstall prompt's and the feed alert's button rows sit in `ui.horizontal`, like the rows in the release-notes, launcher-update and Settings dialogs already do, so they take only a row's height.

No user-facing strings were added, so the i18n catalogs are unchanged.

## Test

`the_uninstall_prompt_keeps_its_own_size_after_a_taller_dialog` opens Settings, closes it, opens the uninstall prompt from PhotoCraft's … menu and checks the buttons follow the text. Before the fix they sat 243 px below it; after, within the 20 px the layout asks for. It also saves a `uninstall-prompt-dark` snapshot with `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_SNAPSHOTS`.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, wasm).

title: Keep feed repo renames inside storytold, and never install without a checksum
author: XianZheYang
body:
Fixes #90, both parts, on every platform. The report describes conditional supply-chain risk, not a live compromise, and the live feed today has no repo renames and a SHA-256 for every file of every app, so nothing that installs now stops installing.

## 1. A repo rename can't leave `storytold`

`Feed::repo_for` followed any `repo_renames` entry whose names merely looked like `owner/name`, so a compromised feed could point an app (or the launcher's own self-update) at another account's repository and ship matching links and checksums; the URL-prefix and SHA-256 checks would then vouch for the attacker's files. AGENTS.md already says downloads come only from `https://github.com/storytold/<app>/releases`.

- `catalog::GITHUB_OWNER` names the account, and `RawRepoRename::into_rename` drops a rename unless both names are under it (case-insensitive), so a move within `storytold` (a repo renamed) still works and a move out of it is ignored. The feed's entry for the app then no longer matches the repo the launcher trusts, and the existing fallback asks GitHub.
- The existing rename test now moves within `storytold`; a new one checks that renames to another account, in either direction, are dropped and the app stays on its catalog repo.

## 2. No checksum, no install

`install::download` accepted a release with neither a per-file digest nor a `SHA256SUMS.txt` line and fell back to checking the size only, with a note appended after the install had already run. Self-update used the same path. A same-length altered file would have passed.

- `download` now refuses before fetching anything, with an error the user can act on: "the release publishes no checksum for `<file>`, so it can't be verified and wasn't installed. Try again later, or report it on GitHub." A `SHA256SUMS.txt` that exists but can't be fetched was already an error, so a network hiccup still never downgrades the check.
- With a checksum always in hand, the size-only machinery goes: `http::download` takes the SHA…

title: linux: fix unresponsive Flatpak sandbox with enhanced D-Bus permissions, cleanup and stripping
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
# Fix Flatpak unresponsiveness for ArtCraft Launcher

## Problem
The `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` flatpak becomes unresponsive due to:
1. Missing D-Bus service permissions causing the app to hang on `do_epoll_wait`
2. Development artifacts left in the binary causing sandbox conflicts
3. Missing cleanup section in the flatpak manifests

## Root Cause Analysis
The app logs show:
```
[2026-10-12T04:26:17Z WARN  artcraft_launcher] no tray icon: D-Bus connection error: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown
```

The app tries to:
- Connect to `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` for tray icons
- Use D-Bus services for notifications
- Access GPU resources via DRI

A StatusNotifierItem must own a bus name before a watcher can claim it, so without
`--own-name` the tray/notification client waits forever on a reply that never comes, and the UI
freezes in `do_epoll_wait`.

## Solution
Both manifests were updated identically (the "keep finish-args identical" contract between them is
preserved):
`packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher.yml` and
`packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher.bundle.yml`.

### 1. Enhanced D-Bus permissions
- `--own-name=ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` — register the app's own bus name
- `--own-name=ai.artcraft.app` — the app's alternate identifier on the session bus
- `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.DBus` — talk to the bus daemon itself (required before any other bus call resolves)
- `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierWatcher` — alternative (non-KDE) tray icon watcher
- Additional desktop services: `org.a11y.Bus`, `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop`

### 2. Cleanup development artifacts
Added a per-module `cleanup` section to remove `*.debug`, `*.pdb`, `*.o`, `*.a`, `*.la`, `*.cmake`,
`/include`, `/lib/debug`, `/share/debug` and `/share/man`.

### 3. Binary stripping
Added `strip --strip-unneeded /app/bin/artcraft-launcher` to remove unnecessary symbols so the
debuginfo…
