title: Reject corrupt and future self-update timestamps
author: MMexicann
body:
A corrupt self-update marker can panic while checking for launcher updates, and a future timestamp can suppress an update beyond the intended 24-hour grace period.

### Reproduction and root cause

Write the release tag and `-9223372036854775808` on the two lines of `<data>/self-update.txt`, then check that same release with `just_updated_to`. The unchecked `now - at` subtraction overflows. A future timestamp also satisfies the old `age < 24h` condition because negative ages were accepted.

### Implementation and coverage

Use checked subtraction and require an age in `0..24h`. Invalid or future markers no longer suppress updates. The existing grace period for a genuinely recent matching release is preserved. The production change is one line, with no new dependencies or user-facing strings.

Two regression tests use temporary marker files: the minimum signed timestamp reproduces the overflow; a day-ahead timestamp and `i64::MAX` reproduce incorrect suppression. The existing tests retain coverage for recent markers, other release tags, and expiry.

- Before the fix, `cargo test --workspace self_update_timestamp` failed both new tests: arithmetic overflow and incorrect acceptance of a future timestamp.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: **all four steps passed** — formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests (**285 passed, 2 existing ignored**), and core/web Wasm checks.
- Both new timestamp regressions passed in the full suite.

### Platforms and safety

Validation runs on Windows x64 GNU with Rust 1.99.0, using workspace TEMP/TMP and disabling incremental compilation for sandbox filesystem restrictions. Linux, macOS and FreeBSD runtime execution are not available locally. No real installation or privileged installer is used. Packaging is unchanged, so shellcheck/actionlint and packaging validation are not applicable.

This only validates the existing self-update grace marker. Approved first-party sources, mandatory SHA-256 verific…

title: Stop download retry loops when a partial file cannot be removed
author: MMexicann
body:
An oversized cached partial download can leave its worker spinning until the user cancels if the partial file cannot be removed, for example while another process holds a Windows file lock.

### Reproduction and root cause

Create a `.part` file larger than the expected release size, then hold it open without delete sharing on Windows. `fetch_resuming` sees the oversized file, ignores the removal error, and immediately repeats with the same file size. No download attempt can make progress. A directory at the partial-file path exercises the same failed removal on Unix.

### Implementation and tests

Propagate the removal failure through the existing download file error format. The user receives the filesystem error instead of an endless local retry loop. The blocked file remains intact, and a later retry can recover after the lock or filesystem problem is resolved. This changes one production line.

Two tests use temporary files and a loopback HTTP server:
- An ordinary oversized partial is removed, the download restarts from byte zero, and the published SHA-256 is verified.
- A partial that cannot be removed returns a file error and remains intact. The Windows fixture uses an owned file handle; the Unix fixture uses a directory. A cancellation watchdog bounds the old loop so the regression cannot hang the suite.

Before the fix, `cargo test --workspace oversized_partial` produced **1 passed, 1 failed**: normal recovery passed, while the blocked-file case returned `cancelled` only after the watchdog stopped its loop. `git diff --check` passed. `cargo xtask ci`: **all four steps passed** — formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests (**285 passed, 2 existing ignored**), and core/web Wasm checks. Both new download regressions passed, including the Windows file-lock case.

### Platforms and safety

Validation runs on Windows x64 GNU with Rust 1.99.0, with workspace TEMP/TMP and incremental compilation disabled for sandbox filesystem restrictions. Th…

title: macOS: build again after install_dmg gained a replace argument
author: dquimper
body:
## Problem

`main` (since #461, `307efcf`) no longer compiles on macOS:

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 7 arguments but 6 arguments were supplied
   --> crates/native/src/self_update.rs:184:26
    |     install::macos::install_dmg(&LAUNCHER, &file, Some(&existing), None, paths, &…)
    |                                                                         ----- argument #5 of type `bool` is missing
```

#461 added a `replace: bool` argument to `install::macos::install_dmg`, but the two calls in `self_update.rs` weren't updated: the macOS self-update (line 184) and the `the_new_bundle_replaces_the_running_one` test (line 374). `main`'s CI passed, which suggests per-PR CI doesn't build the macOS target.

## Fix

Pass `replace: true` in both calls. The bundle being replaced is the running launcher itself, so self-update writes over it unconditionally, which is how it behaved before #461. With `false`, self-update would depend on the new "already exists and wasn't installed by ArtCraft Launcher" check recognising the launcher's own bundle.

## Testing (macOS arm64)

- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt and clippy pass, and wasm passes.
- `self_update::tests::the_new_bundle_replaces_the_running_one` passes.
- `install::tests::macos_checks::*` are intermittently flaky on this machine with `hdiutil: attach failed - Resource temporarily unavailable` (disk-image mounting contention, not this change; #289 reports the same on unmodified `main`). They pass on rerun: 2 of 3 serial runs passed fully.

author: EternalShade3D

## Why

Portable mode is defined as keeping everything in `ArtCraftLauncherData` next to the exe (AGENTS.md, Windows section). title: docs: point the README's Trunk link at the bundler's site
author: GabrielMatozo
body:
Fixes #462

## What was wrong

`README.md`, "Build from source", linked the bundler as `[trunk](https://trunkrs.dev/)`. That domain no longer serves the bundler: it was re-registered and now serves an unrelated site.

Wayback snapshots of `https://trunkrs.dev/`:

| Snapshot | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-04-01 | `Trunk \| Efficient Web Application Bundler for Rust with Minimal Configuration` |
| 2026-08-24 | unrelated site |
| 2026-10-01 | unrelated site |

## Why not `trunk.dev` as the issue proposed

`https://trunk.dev/` resolves to HTTP 200, but it is a different product: `Trunk — Agent-scale version control` (Balearic Labs LLC), not the Rust/WAsm bundler. Pointing the README there would swap one wrong link for another.

The bundler's own repo is the source of truth for its site:

- `trunk-rs/trunk` README: *"Head on over to the [Trunk website](https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk)"*
- `trunk-rs/trunk` `site/config.toml`: `base_url = "https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/"`

So this PR uses `https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/`.

## Change

One line in `README.md`:

```diff
-The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunkrs.dev/):
+The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/):
```

A repo-wide search found no other occurrence of the old URL. Docs-only change, so `cargo xtask ci` is unaffected.

title: macOS: skip wgpu's indirect-call validation on Intel Macs
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Fixes #344, fixes #516, fixes #561.

On Intel Iris and Iris Pro Macs the launcher exits at startup. Metal's compiler fails on wgpu's indirect-validation compute shader (`wgpu_core::indirect_validation ... Compiler encountered an internal error`), the device is lost, and eframe exits with `WGPU error: Parent device is lost`.

## Cause

egui-wgpu's default instance flags are `InstanceFlags::from_build_config().with_env()`, which in wgpu 30 include `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL`, so `request_device` compiles the validation shaders. The macOS `wgpu_options()` returned that default unchanged.

## Fix

On x86_64 macOS builds, `wgpu_options()` removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` and then applies `with_env()`, so `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` still turns it on. The launcher issues no indirect draws or dispatches. Apple silicon, Windows and Linux keep wgpu's default. This copies PhotoCraft's fix and its `skips_indirect_validation` helper (storytold/photocraft#3171, `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`).

No Intel Mac was available here. In #561, pauerbuk reported that `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=0` makes 0.4.1 start and work on an Intel Iris Mac mini; this change makes that the default. Thanks to pauerbuk for the workaround.

#514 has no log and stays open. #38 (`metal3.2` on OpenCore Legacy Patcher systems) is a different fault and stays open.

## Tests

- `intel_macs_skip_the_indirect_validation_shaders`: the helper returns true for an Intel Mac and false for Apple silicon, Windows, Linux and FreeBSD.
- `intel_macs_create_the_device_without_indirect_validation` (macOS): on x86_64, `wgpu_options()` lacks the flag unless `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` turns it on; on Apple silicon it keeps wgpu's flags. Built for x86_64 and run under Rosetta (`cargo test -p artcraft-launcher --target x86_64-apple-darwin`), it fails on `main` with `InstanceFlags(DEBUG | VALIDATION | VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL)` and passes with the change, with the variable unset, `1` and `0`.

title: Don't offer Resume for a download that never connected
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #576.

`start_job` rewrites every `PAUSED` the user didn't ask for into *"The download paused because the connection keeps dropping. Press Resume to continue where it stopped."*, whether or not any bytes arrived.

When nothing arrived:

- there is no part file, so `report_partial` emits `Event::Paused { download: None }` and the card shows the plain **Install** button. The text named a Resume control that isn't on screen.
- "the connection keeps dropping" describes a connection that was never made.

## The change

`start_job` now asks the same question `report_partial` does — does a part file hold any bytes? — and picks the text to match:

- **bytes on disk** → unchanged wording, Resume really is there;
- **nothing on disk** → *"The download didn't start: nothing could be reached, so there is nothing to resume. Check your connection and try again."*

The choice moved into `paused_message(resumable: bool)` so it can be tested on its own.

## Verified on Windows

ArtCraft Launcher built from this branch, Windows 11 Pro 25H2, run in portable mode so the test used its own data folder.

1. Start once with a network so the release cache fills.
2. Restart with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9` and `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9` (nothing listens on port 9).
3. Press Install on FigCraft 0.7.0, keep the default folder.

The log shows the retries ending as the issue describes:

```
figcraft-0.7.0-windows-x64.msi: couldn't connect: io: ... (os error 10061); retrying   [x8]
figcraft-0.7.0-windows-x64.msi: no progress after 8 attempts; pausing

No `.part` file exists anywhere under the data folder afterwards, so `partial_bytes` returns `None` and the new branch is the one taken. The toast now reads *"The download didn't start: nothing could be reached…"*, and the card returns to **Install**, which is consistent: there is no Resume button, and the text no longer claims one.

title: fix(notes): draw the markup in release notes instead of its markers (#591)
author: GabrielMatozo
body:
Closes #591.

## What was wrong

`draw()` classified a line as heading, bullet or text and then painted the whole line in one
`ui.label`, so every inline marker reached the screen as typed. The screenshot in the issue shows
exactly that: a file reference drawn as `From [`docs/scorecard.md`](https://github.com/…) (done /
partial / missing):` — backticks and brackets as characters, the URL wrapped mid-path because it
was plain text — and bullets reading `**Tools:** 29 / 13 / 1`.

## What this does

- `spans()` splits a line into its inline pieces (`Plain`, `Bold`, `Code`, `Link`), and `inline()`
  draws them: bold in Inter 600, code in Geist Mono, and a link as a hyperlink carrying its own
  label, so the URL no longer has to be read — or wrapped — inside the note.
- A heading draws no emphasis, so it gets its text with the markers dropped.
- A link is clickable only when `core::release::safe_web_link` accepts it, exactly like the
  pull-request link beside it; otherwise its label is drawn as plain text. A release body is
  hostile input.
- Only the markup a release body actually carries is recognised. A lone `*`, a marker pair with a
  space inside it, an unclosed marker and `[text](url "title")` all stay literal, so text such as
  `29 * 3` or `snake_case_name` keeps every character.
- A line with no markup keeps the single label it had, so the fold ("Show N more changes"), the
  dialog's own zoom and every other line are untouched.

Nested emphasis is the one thing left half-rendered: `***x***` draws the inner run and leaves the
outer asterisks visible, rather than growing a full inline-markdown engine. No character is dropped.

## Two things the first draft got wrong

- The link search runs again after every unmatched `[`, so searching to the end of the line cost a
  scan per bracket: **1.07 s on a 64 KiB line of `[`**, the `release::MAX_NOTES` ceiling, and a line
  is parsed twice per frame. The label and address searches now stay inside a small window — a link
  …

title: Survive a lost graphics device: open a new window instead of crashing (#274)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #274.

## Cause

The launcher's window draws with a wgpu device. A driver reset can lose that device: for example when the PC wakes from sleep, the GPU driver recovers from a hang, or the OS kills a long submission. The launcher never handled that:
- **egui-wgpu panics** on the next frame with shapes, in `renderer.rs:984`: "Failed to create staging buffer for index data". That's this issue's message.
- **wgpu's default uncaptured-error handler panics too**, on the errors that follow a loss.

PhotoCraft had the same crash (storytold/photocraft#1215, fixed in storytold/photocraft#6464). The launcher can do better than PhotoCraft does, though: it already reopens its window in a loop for the tray, and each new window gets a fresh device.

## Change

- **New `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/gpu_health.rs`, with `WindowGpu`:**
  - `set_device_lost_callback` records the loss.
  - `on_uncaptured_error` logs errors instead of panicking.
  - `lost()` polls the device once per frame, without blocking. `Device::poll` panics on a lost device, so the poll is guarded with `catch_unwind`, and a panic there counts as a loss.
- **`Shell::ui`:** once the device is lost, the frame draws nothing (`ctx.graphics_mut` is cleared), so egui-wgpu has nothing to upload. The shell sets `Launcher::reopen_window` (keeping the window hidden if it was) and closes the window. The close handler doesn't treat that close as "go to the tray".
- **The window loop in `main`:** when `reopen_window` is set, the next `run_native` pass starts straight away, with a new window and a new device. `ReopenBudget` allows that at most 3 times in 10 minutes, so a GPU that keeps failing can't open windows in a loop. Past the budget, the launcher carries on in the tray (or exits where there's no tray), as when the window is closed.
- **Strings:** no new user-facing text; only log lines.

## Tests

- **`gpu_health::tests::a_destroyed_device_reads_as_lost_without_panicking`:** `Device::destroy()` then reads as lost, and …

title: fix(windows): repoint the start-at-login entry when the launcher has moved (#595)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #595.

On Windows, start at login is a `HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run` value that stores the launcher's full exe path. `is_enabled` only checks that the value exists, so after the launcher is reinstalled or moved to another folder the toggle still shows "on" while the value points at an exe that is no longer there. That matches the report: Task Manager lists the entry, "Open file location" is greyed out, nothing starts at login, and turning the option off and on again fixes it (the toggle rewrites the value with the current path).

Changes:
- `login::refresh()`, called once at startup in the primary instance: if the `Run` value exists and differs from what this exe would write, it rewrites the value through `set_enabled(true)` and logs the old and new value. If start at login is off, nothing changes.
- `run_value(exe)` builds the value in one place, shared by `set_enabled` and `refresh`. `repointed(stored, exe)` decides whether a rewrite is needed.
- Windows only, because the report is about Windows. macOS and Linux `set_enabled` paths are unchanged.

The repaired entry takes effect from the next login after the launcher has been opened once (for example from the Start menu), since a stale entry can't start the launcher itself.

Tests: `run_value_quotes_the_path_and_starts_hidden` checks the value format, and `a_run_value_for_an_old_location_is_repointed_at_this_one` checks that a value for another path gets rewritten and the current one is left alone.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * The launcher now checks its Windows startup entry whenever it starts as the primary instance. If the entry points to a program that no longer exists, it is updated to the current launcher location. Valid entries are left unchanged, and the launcher continues to start hidden. This helps keep automatic startup working after the launcher is moved or updated.

title: feat(install): app/system default in the Install dialog, free-space warning, install location in details
author: Belligerently
body:
## What this does

Three related improvements to installing apps, all in the Install dialog and the details drawer.

**1. The Install dialog offers the app default, the system default, or a custom folder.**
Today, once a default folder is set in Settings, the dialog has no way to put one app back in the
system's usual place: "Use default" means the launcher's default. The dialog now shows three choices
(`widgets::cells`, like the theme picker):

- **App default**: the folder from Settings, shown by name (or "same as the system default" when none is set)
- **System default**: the system's usual place, even when Settings has a default folder
- **Custom folder**: the folder field and Browse…, plus "Make this my default install folder"

`InstallLocations` gains a `system` set for apps that keep the system's place; `folder()` returns
`None` for them. It is `#[serde(default)]`, so existing settings load unchanged. The dialog opens on
whatever the app used last. When a translation is too wide for one row, the options stack.

**2. Free space on the target drive.**
The dialog shows how much room the drive under the chosen folder has, and warns (without blocking)
when there is less than about twice the download. That's roughly enough room to download and then
unpack. A folder that doesn't exist yet is measured at its nearest existing parent. This goes through a new
`Host::free_space` (default `None`, so the web build shows nothing) and
`native::paths::free_space`, which uses `fs4` (MIT OR Apache-2.0) so the native crate stays free of
`unsafe`.

**3. Where an installed app lives.**
An installed app's details drawer gets an "Installed at" box with the path (selectable) and the
existing Show in Finder/Explorer action (`Command::Reveal`).

title: feat: add support for updating third-party apps
author: MegaTheLEGEND
body:
# Add support for third-party apps

## Summary

This PR introduces a feature that may be somewhat controversial: support for third-party applications in Craft Launcher.

Many AI reimplementation projects have similar or identical release-page structures, making them good candidates for integration into Craft Launcher.

Third-party app support is **disabled by default**. Users must explicitly enable the feature by navigating to **Settings > Third-Party Apps > Add App** and configuring an application. Until a user does this, the feature remains completely inactive.

**ArtCraft does not provide support for third-party applications.** The UI makes this distinction clear, informing users that external applications are not officially supported by ArtCraft and that responsibility for their maintenance and functionality lies with their respective developers.

### Changes
- Add a custom app system for defining and managing third-party applications.
- Keep third-party app functionality disabled until a user explicitly configures an app.
- Integrate third-party apps into the catalog, detection, installation, and uninstallation workflows.
- Extend the native backend and application protocol to support the new functionality.
- Add settings, dialogs, and views for configuring and managing third-party apps.
- Clearly communicate the third-party support disclaimer in the UI.
- Add translations for the new UI strings across supported locales.
- Update documentation to reflect the new functionality and support boundaries.

The goal is to make third-party applications available to users who explicitly choose to configure them, while preserving the default experience and maintaining a clear distinction between ArtCraft-supported applications and externally maintained projects.

- Tested on Windows and Ubuntu. Both worked as expected.
- `cargo test` passed.

title: portable: install a ZIP that wraps its program in one folder
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2461, where a portable install fails with

> The portable ZIP does not contain the expected executable at its root.

## Cause

`crates/native/src/portable.rs` looks for the executable only at the ZIP root:

```rust
.find(|relative| {
    relative.parent().is_some_and(|p| p.as_os_str().is_empty())
        && relative.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str())
            .is_some_and(|name| app.stems().any(|stem| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&format!("{stem}.exe"))))
})
.ok_or("The portable ZIP does not contain the expected executable at its root.")?
```

A release ZIP almost always wraps everything in one folder — `VectorCraft-1.2.3/vectorcraft.exe` — and those are refused outright.

Searching deeper would not have been enough on its own. Every entry is installed at the path it carries in the ZIP (`destination.join(relative)`, read back from `unpacked.join(relative)`), so the wrapper folder would have been installed too and the program would have landed one level down.

## Change

One wrapping folder is dropped — from the folder the files are read from *and* from the names they are installed under — so a wrapped ZIP installs exactly as one packed flat does. The existing root-level search then works unchanged.

Only when it is unambiguous:

| ZIP | result |
|---|---|
| `App-1.2.3/app.exe`, `App-1.2.3/data/fonts.bin` | wrapper dropped |
| `app.exe`, `data/fonts.bin` | left alone — already flat |
| `App/app.exe`, `README.txt` | left alone — stripping would lose the file beside it |
| `a/app.exe`, `b/fonts.bin` | left alone — nothing unambiguous to strip |

Only the outermost folder goes; a deeper tree keeps its shape.

## Where it lives, and why

The decision is pure path reasoning, so it is in a new `portable_layout` module that is **not** gated, rather than inside `portable`, which `lib.rs` declares `#[cfg(windows)]`. `portable` calls it in one line:

```rust
let (unpacked, files) = crate::portable_layout::unwrap_single_folder(unpacked, files);
```

| Show in Explorer / Reveal in Finder / Open containing folder | `folder-open` |
| Reinstall | `rotate-ccw` |
| Uninstall… | `trash-2`, tinted the theme's red |
| Website | `globe` (already in the repo) |
| GitHub repository | `github` (already in the repo) |
| All releases | `tag` |
| Hide App / Unhide App | `eye-off` / `eye` |

## Why

The menu is a column of similar-looking words, and the two that remove something sit next to the
ones that only open a page. A shape at the start of each row makes the list readable at a glance
and gives Uninstall a colour of its own.

## How

- New `widgets::menu_item()` draws the icon, then the label, inside a row that is exactly as wide
  as its longest label, with a hover that runs to the edge of the menu. A translated label can be
  much longer than the English it was written from, and a row narrower than its label cannot be
  clicked.
- It reports only the label to the accessibility tree, so anything finding a row by name still
  finds it, and screen readers do not have to describe decoration.
- Icons are [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) 0.468.0, ISC, on their own 24 px grid, in `assets/icons/`,
  with `stroke` set to white so the row can tint them the way `assets/social` already does.
- `NOTICE`, `ATTRIBUTION.md` and `assets/icons/README.md` record where each icon came from, and
  `assets/icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt` carries Lucide's ISC notice and its Feather lineage.
- Nothing is drawn as a character, so no font has to carry a symbol.

No behaviour changes: same rows, same order, same actions.

author: Mulyawan-ts
body:
# Add crate-ci/typos spell check to CI

## What

Adds a `typos` job to `ci.yml` and a `typos.toml` config, so a misspelling in a comment, a doc comment, a message or a UI string is caught on the PR instead of living in the tree until someone notices it.

```
crate-ci/typos@685eb3d55be2f85191e8c84acb9f44d7756f84ab # v1.29.4
```

SHA-pinned like the other third-party actions in this repo (`actions/checkout`, `Swatinem/rust-cache`). Runs on `ubuntu-latest`, no Rust toolchain needed, finishes in seconds.

## Why

I ran `typos` over the whole tree first, and it found no English typo, so there is nothing to fix in this PR. That is the point of adding the check: cheap insurance, and the interesting part was the config, not the findings.

## The config, and why it needs one

Two kinds of exemption, both deliberate.

**The translation catalogs are excluded.** `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv` has nine languages in its second column (German, French, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish, Czech, Hungarian, Japanese, Chinese), and `typos` reads every file type. Without the exclusion it reports about 90 correct words as English misspellings. `docs/brand/LICENSE-brand.txt` is excluded too: it is a verbatim trademark licence, not text we are free to edit.

**The prose is British, the code is American.** This repo writes "colour", "centred", "licence", "honoured", "neighbour" in comments and doc comments, but keeps `Color32`, `center()`, "notarized" and "localization" in code and in Apple notary terms. `typos` has one locale per project, so `locale = "en-us"` plus an explicit list of the British spellings in `[default.extend-words]` is the only combination that reads the tree as intended. The i18n tests under `crates/ui-egui/tests/` assert on the same translations, so they need `[default.extend-identifiers]` for the German, French, Spanish and Polish words that appear in UI labels.

title: fix(linux): honour desktop X11 scale factor and propagate to launched…
author: ccsimenson
body:
## Summary

On Linux, `winit`'s X11 backend ignores desktop DPI settings (`Xft.dpi`, `GDK_SCALE`, `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`) when `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is unset and instead computes the scale factor from the monitor's EDID physical millimeter dimensions reported by XRandR.

Many HDMI monitors and TVs (such as Samsung 16:9 displays) encode their aspect ratio (`160 mm × 90 mm`, i.e., `16 cm × 9 cm`) in the EDID physical size fields rather than actual physical millimeters. On a `1920×1080` screen reporting `160 mm × 90 mm`, `winit` computes `304.8 DPI` (`scale_factor = 3.1667`), causing ArtCraft Launcher and every Craft Suite app (which force X11 via `with_x11()` for file drag-and-drop) to open at 2x–3x the size of the screen and persist inflated `inner_size_points` to `app.ron` / `ui.json`.

## Changes

1. **`apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs`**:
   - Add `resolve_x11_scale_factor` and `ensure_x11_scale_factor` to resolve `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` on X11 sessions from `Xft.dpi` (`xrdb -query`), `GDK_SCALE`, or `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`, defaulting to `"1"`.
   - Add unit test `x11_scale_factor_prefers_xft_dpi_then_desktop_env_then_one`.
2. **`crates/native/src/process.rs`**:
   - In `command()`, ensure `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` is propagated when `DISPLAY` is set so Craft Suite apps launched from inside ArtCraft Launcher also avoid XRandR EDID DPI inflation even when the launcher itself runs under Wayland.

title: Settings: one folder for the launcher's files, portable installs included
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #775 (reported against SoundCraft, but this part is the launcher's).

That report notes two folders for one app, which is exactly what the code does:

```
~/.local/share/artcraft-launcher/                   logs, installed.json, apps/
~/.local/share/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher/    app.ron
```

`Paths::new` joins `DIR` (`"artcraft-launcher"` off macOS and Windows); eframe picks its own folder from the app id, `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`. Two independent derivations, so the launcher's state ends up split.

### The part that is more than tidiness

**A portable install is not portable in its settings.** `portable_root()` sends data and cache under `ArtCraftLauncherData` beside the executable when `portable.txt` is there, but eframe's folder stays in the user's profile. So a launcher carried on a stick writes its window size, egui memory and settings into every machine it runs on, and finds none of it on the next one.

### What changed

`Paths::settings()` is `<data>/app.ron`, and `NativeOptions::persistence_path` points eframe at it, so the state file sits beside the logs and the manifest and follows the portable root with everything else.

One thing worth flagging for review: eframe's doc comment calls that option

> The folder where `eframe` will store the app state.

but the value goes to `FileStorage::from_ron_filepath`, so it is the **file**. Passing the folder would have written the state as a file named after the folder. There is a note where it is set.

Settings an earlier version left in eframe's folder are adopted once:

- nothing where the launcher now keeps them → the old file is copied over;
- something already there → left alone, so a downgrade and a re-upgrade cannot replace newer settings with older ones;
- nothing to adopt, or the same path twice → a no-op, not an error.

The old file is left where it is: it is small, and an older launcher started again still finds its settings.

title: fix(windows): retry busy download renames and log Windows Installer runs
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #686

## Problem
On Windows, no Craft app installs. The error is either `couldn't save the download (Access denied. (os error 5))` or `the Windows Installer stopped with error 1603`. Running the launcher as admin doesn't help.

## Changes
- **`http.rs`**: after the checksum passes, the rename from `.part` to the final file now goes through `rename_retrying`. On Windows only, it retries errors 5 (access denied) and 32 (sharing violation) with backoff (100 ms doubling, about 6 s in total). Antivirus scanners commonly hold a freshly written installer open, which makes the rename fail with exactly this error. This is inferred, not reproduced.
- **`install.rs`**: `msiexec` now runs with `/l*v <package>.log`, and errors other than cancel now end with the log's path. 1603 is the installer's generic failure code, so the log is the only way to find the real cause. The existing 7-day download cleanup removes old logs.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native`: 155 pass. The MSI command argument test is updated for the log flag.
- The Windows-only code is not built locally (C dependencies need `lib.exe`), so the Windows CI job is what compiles it.
- Not yet tested on a real Windows machine. Needs a retest from the reporter, plus the MSI log if 1603 persists.

title: Linux and FreeBSD install: run pkexec and package tools from the system directories
author: aiongg
body:
`pkexec` looks a bare program name up on the caller's `PATH`, and the launcher found `pkexec` itself on `PATH` too. Both now come only from a fixed list of root-owned directories:

- Linux: `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`.
- FreeBSD: the same four, then `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/sbin`, because FreeBSD's packages (polkit's `pkexec` at `/usr/local/bin/pkexec` among them) install there.

What uses the list:

- `run_as_root` hands `pkexec` an absolute path. A bare name is looked up in those directories; a relative path with folders in it is refused. The FreeBSD tree install and removal already pass `/bin/cp` and `/bin/rm` by absolute path.
- The checks that decide which package formats can be installed (`apt-get`, `dpkg`, `rpm`, `dnf`, `zypper`, `pacman`) look in the same directories, so the launcher offers only what it can run.
- `pkexec` is found in the same directories, both where it runs a command and where the launcher decides whether a system-wide install is possible (Linux packages; on FreeBSD, the `/usr/local` tree install, which falls back to `~/.local` without `pkexec`).

Unchanged: `pacman -Si` (run as the user) and the paru/yay hint still use `PATH`.

NixOS: its `pkexec` is the wrapper in `/run/wrappers/bin`, which the list doesn't include, so the launcher treats NixOS as having no polkit. That changes no install choice: NixOS's `os-release` names no `.deb`/`.rpm`/Arch family, so it was offered Flatpak and AppImage before and still is. The same holds for any distro whose `apt-get`, `rpm` or `pacman` live outside the four Linux directories: it loses its native-package install and keeps Flatpak and AppImage.

## Checks

- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-native --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo check -p artcraft-launcher-native --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd` (with `--tests` too): builds; the two `self_update.rs` dead-code warnings it prints come from unchanged code. Not run on FreeBSD itself.

title: Preserve long Retry-After cooldowns across restarts
author: MMexicann
body:
`FeedThrottle` accepts a 24-hour `Retry-After`, but restarting discarded that valid saved cooldown because `load()` only allowed deadlines twelve hours ahead. A restart one minute after the response could immediately request the feed instead of waiting another 86,340 seconds.

Accept saved deadlines through the supported `Retry-After` maximum plus the existing 50% jitter, using saturating addition at the clock limit. Add regressions for restarts at jitter values 0, 0.5 and 0.99, and for a saved deadline near the clock limit.

Validation:

- Before the fix: all 12 existing throttle tests passed; the new regression failed (0 versus 86,340 seconds remaining).
- The clock-boundary regression reproduces an arithmetic-overflow panic before saturating the guard.
- Native tests: 139 passed, 3 ignored, 1 filtered. The unfiltered initial run fails only the existing Windows junction test because this sandbox denies `mklink`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and native all-targets Clippy with `-D warnings` pass.
- `cargo xtask wasm` passes for both core and web.

title: fix(ui): drop a saved Installed/Updates/Not installed filter on the desktop too
author: akdavid4real
body:
## What happens

After updating to 0.6.0 on Linux (AppImage), the grid shows only the installed apps, with no "Not installed" section and no way to bring the others back. The settings file still holds `filter:Installed`, saved by an older version that had the filter dropdown.

## Why

`LauncherUi::new` already resets a saved filter the toolbar no longer offers (#527, `e00be80`). But the desktop shell builds the UI with `Settings::default()` in `Launcher::new` and swaps the saved file in later, in `Launcher::start`, with `self.ui.settings = settings`. That runs after the reset, so the stale filter stays active.

## Fix

- The reset now lives in one function, `for_this_page`, in `crates/ui-egui/src/app.rs`.
- The new `LauncherUi::set_settings` applies it to settings loaded after start-up. `Launcher::start` calls it.
- New test, `a_saved_filter_loaded_after_start_up_is_dropped_too`: it loads settings with `Filter::Installed` through `set_settings`, then checks the filter is back to `All` and a not-installed app (DeckCraft) is listed. Without the fix the test fails with `left: Installed, right: All`.

Tests that set `settings.filter` directly to bring cards on screen still work, because the reset only applies to loaded settings, not at draw time.

## Checked

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui -p artcraft-launcher --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui`: all pass (61 UI tests, including the new one)

title: fix(linux): links bring the browser in front of the launcher
author: benandez
body:
Closes #698

## Problem
On Linux (esp. KDE Plasma/Wayland) clicking any link in the launcher opened the browser *behind* the window; KWin only flashed it in the taskbar. eframe opens links without an activation token and drops winit's `ActivationTokenDone` event.

## Fix — port of MailCraft #144 (UCS-Care-Group/mailcraft#167)
- `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/browser.rs` (new, Linux/FreeBSD only): takes egui's `OpenUrl` commands out of each frame, asks winit for an activation token per link, then starts `xdg-open` (or `flatpak-spawn --host xdg-open` in Flatpak) with it in `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` + `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID`. Fallback to the old path (`webbrowser`, as eframe did) when: no token within 1 s, `$BROWSER` set, non-http(s) address, or `xdg-open` fails. URLs never logged.
- `main.rs`: on Linux/FreeBSD the window runs on our own winit event loop via `eframe::create_native` + `run_app_on_demand` (thread-local loop reused across the launcher's window passes, as eframe does), wrapped in `WithTokens` to catch the token. Windows/macOS still use `eframe::run_native`.
- `Cargo.toml`: `[patch.crates-io] winit` → `UCS-Care-Group/winit` @ `bb472d9` (0.30.13 + latest-click serial on the token request, which KWin requires). Same patch MailCraft ships; drop when upstream winit does it.
- `flake.nix`: `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit = true` for that git dep.
- Discord deep link and tray menu links unchanged. Tray links are out of scope: `ksni`/`tray-icon` can't receive the panel's activation token (https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/698#issuecomment-6303073053).

## Notes for review
- ⚠️ New git dependency (winit fork under UCS-Care-Group) — maintainer call. Flatpak's `flatpak-cargo-generator` handles git deps; nix build not verified locally (no nix).
- Not smoke-tested in a live session here (an instance was already running); needs a click test on KDE Wayland, GNOME, X11 and Flatpak.

title: Settings: list the languages alphabetically by their own name
author: nikolainyegaard
body:
The Language picker in Settings listed the languages in registry order, which is the order they were added: Русский and 简体中文 first, Deutsch fourth.

## Change

`Lang::for_picker` returns the languages in picker order: English first, as the source language and the fallback, then the rest sorted by their own name with Latin accents folded, so Čeština is under C and Magyar under M. Names in other scripts follow the Latin ones in code point order, which puts Русский and then the CJK languages at the end without a special rule. The order follows the native name even where the picker shows a CJK language's English name because no font for it is installed, so the list does not reorder when a font appears. The registry keeps its order.

## Test

`picker_lists_english_first_then_names_alphabetically` checks the properties rather than a fixed list, so adding a language cannot make it stale: English first, the keys sorted, Čeština before Deutsch, Magyar after Français, Português before Русский, Русский before 日本語.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --lib -- i18n::`: 31 passed
- `cargo clippy -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: Use jiff instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785 (see reference PR storytold/cadcraft#1789).

## Summary
`crates/core/src/time.rs` and `xtask/src/local.rs` carried their own copies of
Howard Hinnant's civil / days-from-civil algorithm (the `719_468` / `146_097`
magic numbers) to turn GitHub timestamps into dates and back. This routes that
through a real date crate.

Because the launcher already depends on **jiff** (0.2, in `ui-egui` for the
system time zone), I used jiff here rather than adding `chrono`, so the tree
keeps a single time crate. jiff is lifted to a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry
and `ui-egui` now takes it with `{ workspace = true }`; `core` and `xtask` get it
the same way.

Replaced functions and their formats:
- `crates/core/src/time.rs`:
  - `parse_rfc3339` — its `days_from_civil` helper now builds a `jiff::civil::Date`
    and measures the days to the epoch. The day-past-month-length rollover the old
    arithmetic allowed (`2026-02-30` → `2026-03-02`) is preserved by adding
    `(day-1)` days to the first of the month, and the rest of the RFC 3339 field
    parsing and validation (including a leap second) is untouched.
  - `civil_from_unix(i64) -> (i64, u32, u32)` — now pure civil-date arithmetic on
    `jiff::civil::Date` (no time zone), feeding `format_date` ("Oct 8, 2026").
- `xtask/src/local.rs`:
  - `rfc3339(i64)` — the local mirror feed's `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` timestamps,
    now via `jiff::civil::Date`.

`core` uses only civil-date math (no time zone), so the wasm build is unaffected;
`web-time` is untouched. `AGENTS.md` gains the rule that time goes through jiff
and nobody hand-rolls calendar math (its `CLAUDE.md` is a pointer to AGENTS.md, so
it was left as-is).

## Testing
- `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-core` — 39 pass, including
  `reads_github_timestamps`, `shows_dates_people_read` and
  `ago_kind_matches_the_english_fallback`, which pin `parse_rfc3339`,
  `civil_from_unix` and `format_date` (epoch, leap day 2000-02-29, offsets).

title: An argument that is not UTF-8 is ignored, not the end of the start-up
author: Hamza0101
body:
`std::env::args` panics on an argument that is not valid UTF-8, and it panics while **collecting** the arguments — before the launcher looks at what it was given. So any start-up with such an argument ended here:

```
$ artcraft-launcher /tmp/café.png --version        # that é as a single Latin-1 byte
[ERROR artcraft_launcher::logging] internal error: panicked at library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "/tmp/caf\xE9.png"
exit 101
```

Measured on `main`, with the argument before or after `--version` or alone — the window never opens, and the launcher's own panic hook files it as an internal error.

A desktop start-up brings along what it brings along: `-psn_0_…` from Finder when a bundle is opened, a file dropped on the icon, an old login entry's leftovers. The launcher already ignores all of it — it looks for `--version`/`-V` and `--hidden` and nothing else — so an argument it cannot read is one it would have ignored anyway. It now comes through `args_os`, and what cannot be read is logged and dropped:

```
[WARN artcraft_launcher] ignoring an argument that is not valid UTF-8: /tmp/caf�.png
artcraft-launcher 0.6.1
```

### Why it matters beyond the tail case

`packaging/linux/package.sh` runs `"$STAGE/usr/bin/$PKG" --version` as the smoke test for every staged build, including under an emulator for a foreign architecture. That check passes or fails on whether the binary can read its own arguments.

### Tests

`apps/artcraft-launcher/tests/arguments.rs`, the app's first integration test — `--version` is the one thing the launcher does without opening a window, so it is what a test can ask for from here:

- `the_version_is_printed_with_arguments_the_desktop_adds` — `--version` and `-V`, alone and after `-psn_0_1234567` and after a file path.
- `an_argument_that_is_not_utf8_is_ignored_like_any_other` (`#[cfg(unix)]`, since it needs an `OsStr` from raw bytes).

With `std::env::args()` put back, the second fails with exit 101 and …

title: fix(windows): self-update runs no PowerShell and installs only files signed like the launcher
author: dotCooCoo
body:
On Windows the launcher finished its own update with a detached `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -Command …` (`crates/native/src/self_update.rs`, `windows_helper`). The script waited for the launcher to exit, ran the new MSI or `Expand-Archive`d the portable zip over the launcher's folder, deleted the download and started the new exe. A hidden PowerShell with an execution-policy bypass, followed by running and deleting a downloaded file, is a sequence antivirus heuristics score, and the command line sits in the signed `artcraft-launcher.exe` as a string. Related: #251.

## Fix

- The update helper is a copy of the launcher, put in `<cache>\launcher-update-helper` and started with `--finish-update`. `main()` hands that flag to the helper before logging, the single-instance claim and the window.
- The helper waits for the old process with `OpenProcess` and `WaitForSingleObject` (`winsafe`; the workspace forbids `unsafe`), then runs `msiexec /i … /passive /norestart` and checks its exit code, or unpacks the portable zip with the checks `portable::extract` already applies to app installs. Then it starts the launcher again.
- The helper finishes only the launcher's own update. The exe must be this launcher's MSI or portable installation, and the helper, the download and the staging folder must be in that installation's cache. The MSI, every program in the portable zip, and the exe it starts must carry a valid Authenticode signature from the helper's own publisher (`verifysign`, through WinTrust). Without these checks, any program could use the signed launcher to run an arbitrary MSI or exe.
- Before it quits, the launcher checks its own signature, the installed exe and the new MSI. A build without a signature now reports "this copy of ArtCraft Launcher isn't signed …, so it doesn't install updates" instead of updating. Release builds are signed.
- A failed update clears the self-update marker, so the next check offers…

title: fix(windows): read a portable app's version without starting PowerShell
author: dotCooCoo
body:
After unpacking a portable app, the launcher compares the exe's ProductVersion with the release (`install.rs`, the portable arm of `install`). `detect::windows::executable_version` read it by starting a hidden `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` that called `FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo`. That costs a PowerShell start on every portable install, and a hidden PowerShell started by a downloaded exe is a pattern antivirus heuristics score. Related: #251.

## Fix

`executable_version` reads the ProductVersion string from the file's VERSIONINFO with `GetFileVersionInfo` and `VerQueryValue` (`winsafe`, since the workspace forbids `unsafe`): in the languages the file lists, then in the string tables .NET's `FileVersionInfo` also tries (040904B0, 040904E4, 04090000). No process is started.

## Tests

On Windows 11 (x86-64), rustc 1.99.1, on top of `main` at `7dc8375`:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all 4 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, wasm); 20 test binaries, 351 tests passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `apps/artcraft-launcher/tests/version_info.rs` reads the launcher's own exe, which `build.rs` gives a VERSIONINFO, and expects `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. PowerShell's `FileVersionInfo` reads the same `0.6.1` from that exe, so the test passes on `main` too.
- `detect::tests::a_file_without_version_info_has_no_version`: a text file named `.exe` and a missing file have no version.
- `detect::tests::the_version_is_looked_for_in_the_usual_string_tables_too`: the order of the string tables, with and without a listed language.
- `detect::tests::a_version_without_a_translation_entry_is_found` writes a minimal program file holding only a VERSIONINFO, with ProductVersion `1.2.3` in the 040904B0 table and no `\VarFileInfo\Translation` entry, and reads `1.2.3` from it. Without the fallback it reads no version.

title: ci: pin GitHub Actions to full commit SHA (SonarCloud S7637)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Pins third-party GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs (with version comments) instead of mutable tags or branches.

Resolves SonarCloud rule **githubactions:S7637** (Security). Mutable refs like `@v2` or `@stable` can be silently repointed by an action maintainer (or attacker who gains access), so pinning to an immutable commit SHA prevents supply-chain tampering.

## Changes
Actions pinned (version preserved in trailing comment for readability/updates):
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` → `@b725eda…` `# stable`
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` → `@2c76c03…` `# nightly`
- `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` → `@d1527c8…` `# v2.9.3`
- `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2` → `@3c63498…` `# v2.1.1`

## Notes
- Already-pinned actions (e.g. `actions/checkout`) were left untouched.
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`/`@nightly` track moving branches; pinning freezes the toolchain commit. Bump the SHA + comment to update.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.
